classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex first-order perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction in the confined plasma, for a single toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis. It is not the cylindrical major-radius component.
items.documentation:
Imaginary part of the radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the imaginary component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the confined plasma. It applies to one toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis and to the radial coordinate component in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The complex radial component is decomposed into real and imaginary parts as:

$$
\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) = \delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) + i\,\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta)
$$

where $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$ is the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction for toroidal mode number $n$, $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is the corresponding [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $i$ is the imaginary unit, $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate, and $\theta$ is the poloidal flux coordinate.

The scope is the confined-plasma region for the specified toroidal mode; it excludes the perturbed magnetic field in the vacuum region, any sum over toroidal mode numbers, and any real-valued instantaneous perturbation obtained after applying a toroidal and temporal phase factor. The radial direction here is the coordinate direction associated with increasing $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$; it is distinct from the major-radius $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity is a local eigenfunction component, not a flux-surface average, volume integral, or magnitude.

Together with the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), this quantity forms the complex radial component $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$. Together with the [poloidal](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) imaginary components, it forms the imaginary vector part of the perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction. The overall complex phase of a linear eigenfunction is arbitrary, so a phase rotation mixes the real and imaginary parts while leaving the represented complex eigenfunction unchanged.

Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary radial component points toward increasing radial flux coordinate $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ for the adopted complex eigenfunction phase.

items.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission of material from plasma-facing surfaces, weighted by the electron contribution of each emitted species after ionization.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission is the rate at which ionization of material released from plasma-facing surfaces adds electrons to the plasma particle balance. It aggregates all emitted fuel, molecular, and impurity species over all plasma-facing surfaces, with each emitted particle weighted by the number of bound electrons it can contribute after full ionization.

The global rate is defined by integrating the emitted particle flux density over the plasma-facing surface area:

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{surf}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf}}} \sum_s \nu_{e,s}\,\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{surf}}$ is the electron-equivalent surface-emission source rate, $A_{\mathrm{pf}}$ is the total plasma-facing surface area, $s$ indexes emitted species, $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the emitted particle flux density of species $s$ at surface position $\mathbf{x}$ directed toward the plasma, $dA$ is a surface element, and $\nu_{e,s}$ is the electron yield of one emitted particle on full ionization. For an emitted atom, $\nu_{e,s}=Z_s$ with $Z_s$ the nuclear charge number; for an emitted molecule or compound particle, $\nu_{e,s}$ is the sum of the nuclear charge numbers of its constituent atoms.

Surface emission includes recycling, delayed outgassing, and physical or chemical sputtering only insofar as the released material returns toward the plasma and is ionized. This quantity is the electron-specific counterpart of source_rate_due_to_surface_emission, is distinct from externally supplied material represented by [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), excludes electron loss by incidence on surfaces, and contributes to [total_electron_source_rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).

Sign convention: Positive when ionization of material emitted from plasma-facing surfaces supplies electron-equivalent particles to the plasma.

items.name: magnetic_field
items.description: Local total magnetic-induction vector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height; it does not select a source contribution, perturbation state, component, magnitude reduction, or evaluation locus.
items.documentation:
Local total magnetic-induction vector is the magnetic flux-density vector at a point, carrying both the local field direction and field strength. It is the unqualified parent quantity before selecting a source contribution, perturbation state, component, scalar reduction, spatial aggregation, or evaluation locus.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the vector resolves into radial, toroidal, and vertical components as

$$
\mathbf{B} = B_R\hat{\mathbf{R}} + B_\phi\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} + B_Z\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is this local total magnetic-induction vector; $B_R$ is its radial projection, $B_\phi$ is its [toroidal magnetic-field component](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), and $B_Z$ is its [vertical magnetic-field component](name:vertical_magnetic_field); and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ are the corresponding basis vectors. The frame is right-handed with $\hat{\mathbf{R}} \times \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}}$; $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies wherever a local magnetic induction is defined, including confined plasma and surrounding vacuum regions, and no particle species or population is selected or aggregated. It is pointwise and vector-valued: it is not the [magnetic field magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude), a flux-surface-average magnetic field, or an extremum such as the [maximum magnetic field](name:maximum_magnetic_field). No cylindrical component, source contribution, perturbation state, or named locus is implied by the unqualified name.

When a [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ is used, $\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}$; $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector potential and $\nabla \times$ is the curl operator, and a gage change affects $\mathbf{A}$ without changing $\mathbf{B}$. Source-qualified fields such as the [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field) and [plasma magnetic field](name:plasma_magnetic_field) are vector contributions of the same kind and add vectorially when they belong to the same electromagnetic state; the [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field) is the toroidal projection of the vacuum contribution. The [reference magnetic field](name:reference_magnetic_field) is a reference total magnetic-induction vector of the same kind, not a source-specific contribution; the [toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis) is the toroidal projection evaluated at the magnetic-axis locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field component is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, assigning two count units to each atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It represents delivered atomic inventory, not the number of free plasma electrons or the ionization state of the helium-3.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here, $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the helium-3 atom delivery rate in atoms per second, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

The quantity includes only helium-3 delivered after breakdown and is cumulative rather than instantaneous. The corresponding instantaneous delivery rate is [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while [accumulated helium-3 prefill count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection) covers delivery before breakdown.

items.name: net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description: Net thermal power transferred from a single breeder blanket module to its coolant, summed over all coolant branches as an enthalpy increase.
items.documentation:
Coolant thermal power of a single breeder blanket module is the net rate at which heat leaves the module through its coolant circuits. It aggregates the thermal energy carried by every coolant branch serving that module, regardless of whether the heat originated from nuclear deposition or absorbed incident radiation.

The defining branch balance is

$$
P_{\mathrm{cool}} = \sum_b \dot{m}_b\left(h_{b,\mathrm{out}} - h_{b,\mathrm{in}}\right)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cool}}$ is the coolant-transferred power, $b$ indexes coolant branches, $\dot{m}_b$ is the mass flow rate in branch $b$, and $h_{b,\mathrm{in}}$ and $h_{b,\mathrm{out}}$ are its inlet and outlet specific enthalpies. The quantity is the coolant-transferred component of thermal power of a breeder blanket module, distinct from source-specific quantities such as [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) and [absorbed radiated power of a breeder blanket module](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

items.name: accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown equivalent-electron inventory of neutral hydrogen delivered by gas injection, with one count unit assigned to each hydrogen atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral hydrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Hydrogen contributes one equivalent electron per atom because its atomic number is one.

$$
N_{H,mathrm{gas}}(t)=Z_H\,\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_H(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{H,\mathrm{gas}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $Z_H=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $\dot{N}_H$ is the neutral-hydrogen injection rate. The corresponding instantaneous rate is [hydrogen source rate due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The accumulation begins at breakdown and excludes hydrogen introduced during prefill; it represents delivered hydrogen inventory rather than the number of free plasma electrons or the ionization-state distribution. It is the post-breakdown component of hydrogen count due to gas injection, distinct from [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count).

items.name: helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of helium-4 delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection, with each helium-4 atom contributing two equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The helium-4 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-4 is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each helium-4 atom contributes two counts because helium has atomic number 2.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}=2$ is helium's atomic number. This is the helium-4 component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating it over time gives the [accumulated helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection). The [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same atomic-number weighting but represents a separate isotope inventory.

Sign convention: Positive when helium-4 gas is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: oxygen_density
items.description: Total number density of oxygen atoms and ions across all charge states, from neutral to fully stripped, giving the local oxygen impurity concentration at a point in the plasma.
items.documentation:
The local oxygen number density $n_\mathrm{O}$ quantifies the total concentration of oxygen impurity per unit plasma volume, encompassing neutral atomic oxygen and all ionic charge states up to fully stripped O$^{8+}$. Oxygen is a ubiquitous low-Z impurity in fusion devices, entering through wall outgassing and vessel conditioning; it contributes to radiative power losses and dilutes the hydrogenic fuel inventory.

The total oxygen density is defined as the sum over all ionization states:

$$
n_\mathrm{O} = \sum_{Z=0}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}$ is the number density of oxygen in charge state $Z^+$, with $Z$ ranging from 0 (neutral) to 8 (fully stripped).

The local density is inferred from passive extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy, charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, and soft X-ray emission tomography. Spatially averaged forms include [line_averaged_oxygen_density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density) (chord integral divided by chord length) and [volume_averaged_oxygen_density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) (integral over the plasma volume). The dimensionless oxygen_fraction relates this local density to the electron density as an impurity concentration measure.

In well-conditioned fusion plasmas the core oxygen density is a small fraction of the electron density; edge concentrations of $10^{15}$–$10^{17}$ m$^{-3}$ are representative of limiter and divertor configurations.

items.name: radial_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Radial flux limiter coefficient is a dimensionless factor that caps radial momentum-flux density at its collisionless free-streaming bound without reversing the flux direction.
items.documentation:
Radial flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on radial momentum-flux density in a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the sign assigned to the radial flux component.

For the radial component, the direction-preserving limited flux is defined by:

$$
F_R = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_R F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_R$ is the limited radial momentum-flux density, $F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is its unconstrained closure value, $F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming bound, and $L_R$ is the radial component of the [flux_limiter_coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). Nonnegative $L_R$ values below unity impose a stricter cap relative to the free-streaming bound.

This quantity is distinct from the [poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient), which limits the poloidal component, while [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) denotes the component-independent momentum-flux limiter.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_flux
items.description: Poloidal neutral particle flux is the net particle crossing rate per unit area normal to the poloidal direction for one neutral species, summed over internal states.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral particle flux is the local signed number flow of one neutral atomic or molecular species around the magnetic axis, divided by the actual area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction. Crossings in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The poloidal projection is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal neutral particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the neutral particle number-flux vector summed over internal states, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local unit vector in the positive poloidal direction. This direction lies in a constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and sums over all its internal states, rather than selecting the state represented by [poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux). The state-resolved contributions sum to this quantity. It is a local net flux per unit area, not an area-integrated arrival rate or an incident-only flux.

This quantity specializes [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) to an oriented surface whose normal is the local poloidal direction. The poloidal direction is geometric and must not be identified with the magnetic-field direction used for [parallel neutral particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles travel clockwise around the magnetic axis in a poloidal plane viewed with the toroidal symmetry axis to the left and increasing $Z$ upward.

items.name: efficiency_of_plant_system
items.description: Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system converts input power or energy into a specified useful output, abstracting over thermal and net efficiency definitions.
items.documentation:
The efficiency of a plant system is a dimensionless performance metric expressing the fraction of input power or energy that the plant converts into a specified useful output. The exact physical scope depends on the efficiency type applied: [thermal efficiency](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system) characterizes heat-to-work conversion across all thermodynamic conversion stages, while [net efficiency](name:net_efficiency_of_plant_system) accounts for the signed ratio of exported electrical power to total plant electrical consumption including recirculating power.

The general defining relation takes the form:

$$
\eta = \frac{W_\text{out}}{W_\text{in}}
$$

where $W_\text{out}$ is the useful output (work, exported electrical power, or heat converted to work) and $W_\text{in}$ is the total input power or energy over the same operating interval.

Efficiency is evaluated from calorimetric heat-flow surveys, electrical generation meters, and auxiliary power consumption measurements across all plant subsystems. For fusion facilities, thermal conversion efficiencies in steam-cycle plants lie in the range 30–45%, and net electrical efficiencies are further reduced by recirculating power fractions for heating, current drive, and cooling systems.

items.name: electron_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description: Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population, representing angular-momentum exchange with other plasma populations for both fast and thermal electrons.
items.documentation:
Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population is the volume-integrated rate of angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb collisions with other plasma populations. It is the electron-specific member of the broader [torque due to collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions) family and parallels [fast torque due to collisions](name:fast_torque_due_to_collisions).

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{dL_{e,\mathrm{coll}}}{dt}
$$

where $\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the net collisional torque on the electron population, $L_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its volume-integrated angular momentum transferred by collisions, and $t$ is time.

This parent covers both fast and thermal electron cases, represented by fast-electron torque due to collisions and [thermal-electron torque due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions). It excludes torque on ions, which belongs to [ion torque due to collisions](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions), and excludes non-collisional torque mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions increase the electron population's angular momentum in the positive rotational sense about the torque axis.

items.name: methane_carbon_13_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate with 10 equivalent electrons assigned to each neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma vessel is the rate at which neutral $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ enters the plasma vessel, counted using the equivalent-electron convention. Each neutral carbon-13-labeled methane molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons.

The constitutive relation between the equivalent-electron source rate and the molecular injection rate is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4} = 10\,\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the carbon-13-labeled methane source rate, $\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the molecule-counted injection rate of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane, and $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ denotes methane with carbon-13 as the carbon isotope.

This quantity applies only to neutral carbon-13-labeled methane crossing into the plasma vessel by gas injection, aggregated over the relevant injection locations as an instantaneous total. It excludes unlabeled methane, other hydrocarbons, gas remaining upstream of the vessel, and accumulated injected amount.

It is distinguished from a molecule-counted [methane source rate](name:methane_source_rate) by the equivalent-electron counting convention: the present quantity is 10 times the corresponding molecule-counted rate for the same carbon-13-labeled methane population. When the corresponding accumulated count is used, this source rate is the time derivative of the [accumulated methane carbon-13 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection) under the same equivalent-electron convention.

Sign convention: Positive when carbon-13-labeled methane enters the plasma vessel.

items.name: current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive
items.description: Vector electric-current-density contribution generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients.
items.documentation:
Current density due to bootstrap current drive is the vector contribution to electric current density generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients. It represents conventional electric-current flow produced by this drive mechanism, before selecting any particular component or projection.

The quantity is scoped to the bootstrap-driven contribution only. It excludes current-density contributions from externally driven current, inductive electric fields, neutral beams, radio-frequency waves, or any total current density that aggregates multiple drive mechanisms.

This parent quantity denotes the full vector bootstrap-current-density contribution. Component or projection quantities are more specific descendants; for example, [parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive) is the field-aligned projection of this vector along the magnetic-field direction, not a synonym for the full vector.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component represents conventional current flowing in the positive direction of that component or projection.

items.name: hard_xray_brightness
items.description: Band-integrated hard X-ray photon radiance received by a channel, normalized by projected collecting area and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation:
Hard X-ray brightness is the photon radiance received from a viewing direction by a channel. It represents photon arrival rate with the photon-energy dependence integrated over the selected hard X-ray band.

The band-integrated photon radiance is defined by

$$
B_{\mathrm{HX}} = \frac{dN_\gamma}{dt\,dA_{\mathrm{proj}}\,d\Omega}
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{HX}}$ is the hard X-ray brightness, $N_\gamma$ is the number of received photons in the selected energy band, $t$ is time, $A_{\mathrm{proj}}$ is projected collecting area, and $\Omega$ is accepted solid angle.

This quantity applies to hard X-ray photons received by a channel and is evaluated separately for each selected energy band. Its aggregation convention is integration over photon energy within that band while retaining normalization by projected area and solid angle. It is a received radiometric quantity, not a local volumetric source term, and it counts photons rather than their deposited or carried energy.

The local production counterpart is hard X-ray emissivity, which describes photon generation per unit volume and solid angle before propagation to the channel. Integrating this brightness over the collecting geometry represented by the [etendue of a hard X-ray detector](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector) gives the received photon rate under the corresponding angular and area acceptance. Unlike [incident soft X-ray radiance](name:incident_soft_xray_radiance), which is energy-weighted, this quantity is photon-count radiance; photon registration probability is a separate detector property described by [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector).

items.name: power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of collisional energy exchange per unit volume for a specified plasma population, species, charge state, or internal state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for a designated target population. It is positive for energy deposited in the target and negative for energy transferred from it.

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the target power density in W m$^{-3}$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume from partner population $b$ to target $a$, and the sum includes the collision partners and subpopulations specified by the quantity's aggregation scope.

The target may be a broad population, as in particle collisional power density, or a species, ion charge state, internal state, or electron population. Aggregated electron and ion quantities include the designated contributing species and states, whereas resolved quantities retain only their specified target, as in [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and internal-state collisional power density.

Sign convention: Positive when the designated target population gains energy from its collision partners.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional power transferred from counter-passing nonthermal particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from counter-passing nonthermal particles to thermal ions of a specified species, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Counter-passing particles follow passing guiding-center orbits whose transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction. This orbit restriction selects the nonthermal source distribution, not the thermal-ion recipient orbits.

For nonthermal source species $a$ and recipient ion species $i$, the contribution is defined by the recipient kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iq,a}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density, $q$ labels the recipient's ionic charge states, $m_i$ is the recipient-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient-ion velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed. The function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion velocity distribution for charge state $q$, and $f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing portion of the nonthermal source distribution. The operator $C_{iq,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to that source. The integral covers all recipient-ion velocities, and angle brackets denote the magnetic-flux-surface average weighted by the volume element between neighboring flux surfaces.

The charge-state sum includes all ionic charge states of the specified recipient species, not all ion species. The recipients are thermal ions, excluding fast-ion recipients; the quantity is their collisional energy source or sink, not their stored energy. In contrast, [charge-state-resolved thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) retains one specified ionic charge state.

This quantity is the counter-passing contribution to the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Adding the corresponding [co-passing contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and trapped contribution, with the same averaging convention, recovers that orbit-summed average.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic energy to the thermal-ion recipients from the counter-passing nonthermal population.

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor
items.description: Nuclear energy deposition rate integrated throughout the material volume of one divertor structure, including neutron and other nuclear heating sources.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of a divertor is the rate at which nuclear interactions deposit energy throughout the material volume of that divertor structure.

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{div}}} q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the nuclear heating power, $q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local volumetric nuclear energy-deposition rate at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the material volume of the divertor, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The quantity applies to one indexed divertor structure and aggregates neutron and all other included nuclear heating sources over its complete material volume. It excludes energy deposited by nonnuclear convective transport, such as [power of a divertor due to convection](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and is distinct from surface power deposited at an individual target, such as [neutral power at a divertor target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target).

items.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: One-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current, including directed-motion contributions.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits. These particles are untrapped and have orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposite to the plasma current.

For a nonrelativistic species, the local pressure is defined by the restricted second velocity moment:

$$
p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{3}\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the counter-passing fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution function, $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space region belonging to counter-passing orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The velocity moment does not subtract the population mean velocity, so directed motion contributes alongside random motion. Only the suprathermal counter-passing population is included; thermal particles, [co-passing fast particles](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and [trapped fast particles](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) are excluded. Contributions from multiple represented fast-particle populations of the specified species add linearly, rather than forming a density-weighted mean; no sum over different species is implied.

The definition retains local spatial variation. A flux-surface average averages this same local moment and is not intrinsic to the quantity's definition.

This is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure). Its component relationship is $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}+2p_{\perp,s})/3$, where $p_{\parallel,s}$ is the [parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and $p_{\perp,s}$ is the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), averaged over the two transverse directions relative to the local magnetic field. The trace combines these components without requiring them to be equal; it is neither a single directional component nor an assumption of an isotropic distribution.

items.name: ethylene_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous injection rate of ethylene (C2H4) gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second with each molecule counted as 16 equivalent electrons.
items.documentation:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon, four-hydrogen molecule used as a gaseous source of both carbon and hydrogen in plasma fueling and wall-conditioning experiments. The source rate is the instantaneous equivalent-electron delivery rate to the plasma vessel, where each molecule is assigned 16 equivalent electrons based on the total atomic electron inventory of the molecular formula.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular injection rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ by

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 16\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2Z_\mathrm{C} + 4Z_\mathrm{H}$, with $Z_\mathrm{C} = 6$ the carbon atomic number and $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ the hydrogen atomic number.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance calibrations and upstream pressure measurements. Its time-integral gives the [accumulated ethylene count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count), which tracks the total equivalent-electron inventory delivered since plasma breakdown. Related molecular and atomic injection rates include [silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate) for SiH4 and [hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) for atomic hydrogen delivery.

Sign convention: Positive when ethylene gas flows from the injection system into the plasma vessel.

items.name: energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description: The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is distinct from the lower and upper bandpass-edge energies.
items.documentation:
The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is the energy counterpart of the [wavelength of detector pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel) and identifies the pixel's spectral-channel assignment rather than the finite width of its accepted band.

For diffraction order $n$, the representative pixel energy is related to the pixel Bragg angle by Bragg's law and the photon energy-wavelength relation:

$$
E_\mathrm{pix} = \frac{n h c}{2 e d \sin\theta_\mathrm{pix}}
$$

where $E_\mathrm{pix}$ is the energy of the detector pixel, $n$ is the diffraction order, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $d$ is the spacing of the diffracting crystal planes, and $\theta_\mathrm{pix}$ is the Bragg angle associated with the pixel.

This representative energy is the calibrated spectral-channel value selected by the spectrometer energy scale; it need not equal the arithmetic midpoint between the [lower bound energy of detector pixel](name:lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel) and the [upper bound energy of detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which define the edges of the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

items.name: surface_area_of_divertor_tile
items.description: Geometric area of the plasma-facing surface of an individual divertor tile, defining the surface over which incident plasma loads are spatially integrated.
items.documentation:
The tile surface area is the geometric area of the plasma-facing wetted surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a property of the tile geometry, independent of the incident heat, particle, or current load.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm tile} = \int_{S_{\rm tile}} dA
$$

where $S_{\rm tile}$ is the plasma-facing tile surface and $dA$ is an elemental surface area. The result provides the geometric denominator for converting an integrated load into a tile-averaged surface density, such as the [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

This quantity applies to one tile and must not be confused with the [wetted area of a divertor target](name:wetted_area_of_divertor_target), which characterizes a target-level deposited-flux region, or the total wetted area of the divertor summed over multiple targets.

items.name: lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron lithium source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected lithium atom contributing three equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The lithium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral lithium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the lithium-specific component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), rather than the raw lithium-atom delivery rate.

For lithium, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the raw lithium atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's dimensionless atomic number.

The equivalent-electron convention assigns three source counts to each injected lithium atom and excludes other gas species. This rate is the time derivative of the corresponding accumulated lithium count; its atomic-number weighting distinguishes it from the [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

Sign convention: Positive when lithium is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Number density of nitrogen ions evaluated at the radial position of the internal transport barrier, where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport sustains steep impurity density gradients within the confined plasma.
items.documentation:
Nitrogen (atomic number $Z = 7$) is a medium-Z impurity that is seeded into fusion plasmas for radiative power exhaust control and divertor heat-load mitigation. This quantity gives the local number of nitrogen particles per unit volume at the radial reference position of an internal transport barrier (ITB) — a narrow region within the confined plasma where cross-field turbulent transport is locally suppressed, enabling steep radial gradients to develop and persist. Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is specified separately, it represents the nitrogen ion density summed over all ionization states, consistent with the parent [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

In hot plasma core conditions above approximately 1 keV, nitrogen is found predominantly in high ionization states ($N^{5+}$–$N^{7+}$). Within an ITB, neoclassical impurity transport — including temperature-screening and centrifugal effects on the impurity density profile — can drive strong inward or outward peaking of $n_\mathrm{N}$ at the barrier radius, with direct consequences for the local $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ and radiated power balance.

Nitrogen density in the plasma core is measured by charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, which resolves individual charge states whose sum yields the total impurity density; transport analysis then extracts the value at the ITB reference location from the fitted profile. Compare with [neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) for a noble-gas impurity of similar use, and with [nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) for the corresponding boundary value of the same species.

items.name: accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3), expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units per molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative number of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, converted to an equivalent-electron count. It is the post-breakdown contribution to ammonia_deuterated_count, distinct from the prefill contribution [ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count).

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = 10N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the cumulative neutral-molecule count after breakdown, and $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and deuterium. This is a bookkeeping quantity, not the number of free electrons in the plasma and not an instantaneous injection rate.

items.name: neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective vector velocity at which neutral particle momentum is advectively transported in edge-plasma fluid models, aggregated over all neutral species and excited states as a transport closure coefficient distinct from the actual neutral particle flow velocity.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum convection velocity is the effective bulk vector velocity appearing in the non-diffusive, advective contribution to neutral momentum transport in edge-plasma and scrape-off-layer fluid models. It encapsulates the net effect of charge-exchange, ionization, and recombination reactions on the aggregate neutral momentum balance across all neutral species and excited states, serving as a transport closure coefficient rather than the physical flow speed of any individual neutral population.

In multi-fluid edge-plasma transport frameworks, the total neutral momentum flux is decomposed into a diffusive part proportional to the local momentum-density gradient and a convective (pinch-like) part proportional to the momentum density:

$$
\mathbf{F}_p = -D_p \nabla p_n + \mathbf{V}_c \, p_n
$$

where $D_p$ is the neutral momentum diffusivity and $p_n$ is the neutral momentum density. The convection velocity $\mathbf{V}_c$ (this quantity) drives advective momentum transport independently of the local gradient, functioning as a neutral momentum pinch.

The quantity is computed in fluid neutral transport solvers as a closure derived from atomic physics rate coefficients and the local plasma state. Its directional projections include the radial_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($R$ component) and the vertical_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($Z$ component) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The analogous charge-state-resolved quantity is [radial_neutral_state_effective_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity). The parent momentum_convection_velocity establishes the general momentum-flux decomposition framework from which this neutral-species specialization is derived.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description: Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination, resolved by neutral product species and internal quantum state.
items.documentation:
Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the surface flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state that are produced by recombination at the wall and cross the wall surface away from the wall. It is resolved by neutral product species and by the internal quantum state of that product.

For neutral product species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, with $\hat{\mathbf n}_w$ the unit normal directed from the wall material into the adjacent plasma, the outgoing recombination contribution is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,out}}_{n,\alpha} = \int_{\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w > 0} (\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w)\, f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}(\mathbf v)\, d^3\mathbf v
$$

where $\mathbf v$ is neutral-particle velocity and $f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}$ is the velocity-space distribution function at the wall for neutral recombination products of species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, normalized so that its velocity integral gives the corresponding local neutral-product number density.

This quantity includes only the emitted, outward wall-normal component of neutral recombination products in the specified internal state. Aggregating over internal states for the same neutral product species gives the [neutral particle flux at wall due to recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the broader internal-state-resolved recombination-flux family is internal state particle flux at wall due to recombination. The distinct inward wall-normal counterpart is [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) and is not included here.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral recombination products cross the wall surface in the direction of the wall normal from the wall material into the adjacent plasma.

items.name: line_averaged_boron_density
items.description: Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all boron ionization states, giving a chord-averaged measure of elemental boron impurity content.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all ionization states of boron, so it represents the chord-averaged elemental boron impurity content rather than a local point value.

The line average over a chord of path length $L$ is defined by the path integral of the local charge-state-summed boron density along arc length $l$:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{5} n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)\, dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell}$ is the line-averaged boron density, $n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)$ is the local boron number density in ionization state $z$ at position $l$ along the chord, $z=0$ denotes neutral boron, $z=5$ denotes fully stripped B$^{5+}$, and $L$ is the total path length used for the average.

This quantity is a chord average of the charge-state-summed elemental [boron density](name:boron_density); it is not a charge-state-resolved boron density and does not exclude neutral boron. It differs from [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), which averages the same elemental density over the confined plasma volume.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume to fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the counter-passing particle distribution.
items.documentation:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the flux-surface-averaged angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the counter-passing particle distribution. It is a component-resolved specialization of [torque density](name:torque_density).

Its relation to the local collisional torque-density vector is

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi} \right\rangle
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ denotes this averaged toroidal component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the [counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque-density vector](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Angle brackets denote the volume-weighted average over an infinitesimally thin shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The counter-passing restriction applies to the contributing particle distribution; the receiving population is the fast electrons. Co-passing and trapped contributions are excluded. Torque delivered to bulk thermal electrons is a distinct quantity, represented by [toroidal counter-passing thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Flux-surface averaging retains torque per volume rather than producing a volume-integrated torque.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged collisional torque received by the fast electrons has a component toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per plasma volume to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions with a specified ion species.
items.documentation:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-ion collisional torque density is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions with a specified ion species.

It is related to the full [counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) by

$$
\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}\cdot\hat{\phi} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the averaged toroidal torque density, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the local collisional torque-density vector acting on counter-passing fast ions, and the angle brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic flux surface. The subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{cp}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify ions, the counter-passing restriction, and collisions, respectively. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

The orbit restriction applies to the fast-ion distribution, not to the collision partners. Co-passing and trapped fast-ion contributions are excluded; co-passing contributions belong instead to [co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Charge-state contributions are summed at the species level, rather than resolved for one ionic charge state, while different collision-partner species remain separate.

This is a toroidal component of [torque density](name:torque_density), not the full vector or a volume-integrated torque. The local toroidal projection is taken before flux-surface averaging.

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional torque acting on the fast ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions at the magnetic axis, combining all ionization states in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis is the local bulk-flow component of argon ions projected onto the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It combines Ar+ through Ar18+ and excludes neutral argon; the magnetic axis is where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ are toroidal velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ is the local number density in m$^{-3}$, and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the magnetic-axis coordinates in m. The denominator corresponds to the charge-state-summed [argon density at the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis); the species and locus semantics parallel [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the charge-state-averaged argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, along $+\hat{\phi}$.

items.name: accumulated_neon_count
items.description: Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons; each injected neon atom contributes ten equivalent electrons.
items.documentation:
Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown is the time integral of the neon atom injection rate due to gas injection, weighted by the neon atomic number. It is a species-specific accumulated count expressed in equivalent electrons, so each injected neon atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ equivalent electrons.

The accumulated neon count $N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation time, $t'$ is the integration time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}$ is the neutral-neon atom injection rate due to gas injection, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the number of electrons in a neutral neon atom.

The scope is neon supplied by gas injection during the interval from plasma breakdown to the evaluation time; the aggregation is cumulative over injected neon atoms, with equivalent-electron weighting applied per atom. It excludes neon present before breakdown, neon supplied by non-gas-injection sources, retained inventory, pumped-out amount, and charge-state-resolved plasma neon populations.

This quantity is the accumulated gas-injection counterpart of the species neon count convention, with the additional accumulation interval and equivalent-electron weighting. It follows the same accumulated equivalent-electron convention as [accumulated krypton count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) and [accumulated ammonia count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count); a neutral-neon atom count without equivalent-electron weighting is obtained by dividing by $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge
items.description: Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population. It is a normalized volume average representing the global mean ionization level of that selected charge state.

For ion species $i$, the volume-averaged ion charge is defined by

$$
\langle Z_{\mathrm{dom},i} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\Omega}\int_\Omega Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [ion charge](name:ion_charge) number of the dominant ionization state of species $i$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega$ is the confined plasma volume, and $V_\Omega$ is the volume of $\Omega$.

The population is one specified ion species; if the species represents a lumped-ion population, the same definition applies to that lumped population. The charge-state convention is dominant-state selection: the quantity is not a charge-state sum and is not the density-weighted mean over all charge states.

This quantity differs from [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number), which represents the density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states of the ion species. It also differs from [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), which is a particle population density rather than a charge number.

items.name: halo_current
items.description: Halo current in the halo plasma region during a disruption is the electric current vector carried by the halo plasma on open magnetic field lines between the last closed flux surface and the first wall. Its poloidal and toroidal components are obtained by integrating the halo current density over oriented cross sections of the halo region.
items.documentation:
Halo current in the halo plasma region during a disruption is the electric current vector carried by the halo plasma flowing on open magnetic field lines between the last closed flux surface and the first wall. It resolves into a poloidal component and a toroidal component, each obtained by integrating the halo current density over an oriented cross section of the halo region.

The component currents are surface integrals of the halo current density, and the current vector is their sum along the corresponding unit directions:

$$
\mathbf{I}_\mathrm{h} = I_{\mathrm{h},\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta + I_{\mathrm{h},\phi}\,\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}, \qquad I_{\mathrm{h},a} = \int_{S_a} \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a\,dS,\quad a\in\{\theta,\phi\}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}$ is the halo current density, $S_a$ is an oriented cross section of the halo region with positive normal $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is tangent to increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The poloidal angle $\theta$ is the angular coordinate in the meridional plane of that $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame about the chosen magnetic-axis reference and is distinct from the toroidal angle $\phi$.

The scalar coefficient $I_{\mathrm{h},\theta}$ is [poloidal_halo_current](name:poloidal_halo_current) and $I_{\mathrm{h},\phi}$ is [toroidal_halo_current](name:toroidal_halo_current). This integrated current vector is distinct from halo_current_density, the local field $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}$ prior to integration over $S_a$, and it counts only current carried by the halo plasma itself, excluding current confined to passive conducting structures after path closure outside the halo region.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal component is directed along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ and the toroidal component is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
items.description: Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma. It describes the beam's post-propagation transverse polarization state, not the incident state or the ellipse orientation.
items.documentation:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma is the ellipticity of that beam. It characterizes the relative electric-field semiamplitudes of the post-propagation transverse polarization ellipse.

The ellipticity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{b}{a}
$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the polarization ellipticity, $a$ is the major-axis semiamplitude of the electric-field polarization ellipse, and $b$ is the signed minor-axis semiamplitude of that ellipse. The magnitude satisfies $|\varepsilon| \leq 1$.

This quantity applies to the polarimeter beam after it has traversed the magnetized plasma and is therefore distinct from the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam). It is a polarization-shape parameter and excludes the orientation of the ellipse; rotation of that orientation is represented by the [Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle). The quantity refers to a single beam polarization state, with no aggregation over distinct beam paths.

Magnetized-plasma birefringence can transform the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) into this post-propagation ellipticity by changing the polarization ellipse during propagation; that change is distinct from Faraday rotation of the ellipse orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field vector rotates in a right-handed sense about the beam-propagation direction.

items.name: maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Upper allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant for a poloidal-field coil, with magnitude and sign defined by one force-combination-matrix row.
items.documentation:
Maximum force of a poloidal-field coil is the upper allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant acting on the coil. It bounds the resultant derived from radial and vertical Lorentz-force components and is distinct from the actual [force of a poloidal-field coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For matrix row $m$, the associated force resultant is defined by

$$
F_m = a_m F_R + b_m F_Z
$$

where $F_R$ is the [radial force of a poloidal-field coil](name:radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), $F_Z$ is the [vertical force of a poloidal-field coil](name:vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), and $a_m$ and $b_m$ are the row-specific force-combination weights. The maximum-force quantity is the upper allowable value assigned to the selected resultant; it is not a separate Lorentz-force component.

Sign convention: Positive when the weighted combination of outward radial force and upward vertical force, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, is positive.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density
items.description: Toroidal current density is the flux-surface-averaged charge flux carried by magnetically trapped fast particles in the toroidal direction, excluding electron and thermal-ion back-currents.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density carried by trapped fast particles is the magnetic-flux-surface average of the toroidal projection of [trapped fast-particle current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). It represents conventional electric-charge transport by nonthermal particles on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}} = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal trapped-fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the local trapped-fast-particle current-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and angle brackets denote the magnetic-flux-surface average. The direction $\hat{\phi}$ follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the trapped portion of the specified species' fast-particle distribution contributes; multiple included fast populations of that species are superposed linearly. Passing fast particles and compensating electron and thermal-ion back-currents are excluded. This is a signed, surface-averaged component, not a local value, a vector magnitude, or the total plasma [current density](name:current_density).

Unlike this direct fast-particle contribution, [toroidal trapped current density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) also includes the collisional drag back-current attributed to trapped particles.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged conventional charge transport by trapped fast particles follows increasing $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: height_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Height of a poloidal field coil is the nonnegative full vertical extent of the rectangular conductor cross-section of an individual active coil element.
items.documentation:
Height of poloidal field coil

The height is the difference between the upper and lower vertical boundary coordinates:

$$
h = Z_{\mathrm{upper}} - Z_{\mathrm{lower}}
$$

where $h$ is the full height, and $Z_{\mathrm{upper}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{lower}}$ are the vertical coordinates of the upper and lower boundaries in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to an individual active coil element's rectangular conductor cross-section; it is not an aggregate over elements or coils. It is the full dimension, not a half-height or the vertical position of the cross-section center, and is distinct from the radial cross-sectional extent represented by the [width of a poloidal field coil](name:width_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For a rectangular cross-section, the height and width determine the [area of a poloidal field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil) as $A = wh$, where $A$ is the cross-sectional area, $w$ is the width, and $h$ is the height.

items.name: radial_total_momentum_flux
items.description: Radial component of total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, combining advective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and turbulent-stress contributions; radial means the increasing-major-radius R direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the radial component of the total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, representing transport of radial linear momentum rather than stored momentum or a force source. The radial projection is the component along $\hat{R}$, the increasing-major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The radial projection of the total momentum-flux tensor through an oriented surface is:

$$
\Pi_R = \hat{R}\cdot\left(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}\right),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}} + p_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $\Pi_R$ is the radial total momentum flux, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal defining the orientation of the crossed surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the mass density of the aggregated total plasma population, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its bulk flow velocity, $p_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

The scope is the total edge-plasma population: contributions from all plasma species and charge states in that population are summed at the level of momentum flux, including convective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and turbulent-stress terms. It excludes single-species or charge-state-resolved momentum fluxes, scalar pressure alone, stored momentum density, and force or torque source densities.

This quantity is the radial projection of [total momentum flux](name:total_momentum_flux). It uses the same radial coordinate convention as [radial momentum flux](name:radial_momentum_flux): radial means increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, not distance from the magnetic axis and not a flux-surface-normal projection; [toroidal total momentum flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is the matched toroidal projection of the same total momentum-flux tensor.

Sign convention: Positive when $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}$ has a component in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description: Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current direction.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current direction.

The source contribution to the evolution of the counter-passing thermal particle number density is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{source}}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is this source rate, $n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged number density of counter-passing thermal particles, $\psi$ is the magnetic flux-surface label, $t$ is time, and the source subscript denotes the explicit particle-source contribution. Positive values represent net particle addition, while negative values represent net particle removal.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population in the counter-passing orbit class and is averaged over magnetic flux surfaces. It is not summed over co-passing or trapped orbit classes and excludes nonthermal particle populations. The corresponding [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) applies the same source definition to the co-passing orbit class.

The broader [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate) aggregates the orbit-population contributions, including this counter-passing component; this quantity therefore represents only the counter-passing contribution rather than the total thermal source.

items.name: trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description: Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class. Trapped particles are those whose parallel velocity reverses along a magnetic field line and therefore undergo bounce motion between mirror points.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}-S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the trapped thermal particle source rate, $S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate of thermal particles entering the trapped orbit class, $S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate leaving it, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface label, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population and the trapped orbit class. It is averaged over each magnetic flux surface and combines all contributing particle source and sink processes; positive values represent net entry into the trapped class, while negative values represent net removal. It excludes co-passing and counter-passing particles.

It is the trapped-orbit contribution to the aggregate [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which combines the source rates of the thermal orbit populations. It is complementary to the [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) and [counter-passing thermal particle source rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), which describe the two passing orbit classes.

items.name: triangularity_of_flux_surface
items.description: Signed dimensionless shape parameter measuring the normalized horizontal displacement of a nested magnetic flux surface’s upper or lower vertical extremum.
items.documentation:
Triangularity of a nested magnetic flux surface is the signed shape parameter formed from the horizontal displacement of an upper or lower vertical extremum, normalized by the surface’s horizontal half-width.

For a selected upper or lower vertical extremum, triangularity is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame by

$$
\delta_s = \frac{R_c - R_s}{a}
$$

where $\delta_s$ is the triangularity, $s$ identifies the selected upper or lower vertical extremum, $R_s$ is its radial coordinate, $R_c$ is the radial midpoint of the flux surface’s horizontal extent, and $a$ is the corresponding horizontal half-width.

This is a geometric parameter of an individual nested magnetic flux surface in an equilibrium plasma. The unqualified quantity covers either vertical extremum and carries no aggregation over multiple flux surfaces, plasma volume, or the plasma boundary.

Triangularity characterizes the radial displacement of a vertical extremum; it is distinct from [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), which describes the ratio of vertical to horizontal extent, and from [outer squareness of a flux surface](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface), which describes corner deformation.

The upper and lower branch-specific quantities are [upper triangularity of a flux surface](name:upper_triangularity_of_flux_surface) and [lower triangularity of a flux surface](name:lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface); each is an instance of this parent quantity with $s$ fixed to the corresponding vertical extremum.

items.name: momentum_source
items.description: Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from a plasma population, represented as a source density resolved by species, internal state, or spatial direction.
items.documentation:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its resolved states. It may retain vector direction or represent a selected component of the momentum-transfer rate.

The area-normalized source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum transferred by the source processes, $A$ is the surface over which the source is normalized, and $t$ is time. Concrete variants may resolve a radial component, an internal state, or an ion charge state, as in [radial momentum source](name:radial_momentum_source) and [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). Population-level quantities may sum the corresponding state-resolved contributions, as for [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source).

items.name: perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure
items.description: Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species is the mean normal kinetic stress perpendicular to the local magnetic field, averaged over internal states.
items.documentation:
Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the mean of its two transverse normal kinetic stresses.
