It is the field-perpendicular component in a gyrotropic description of neutral kinetic stress; the magnetic field supplies the reference direction, not a magnetic confinement force on the neutrals.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse projection of the kinetic pressure tensor:

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp} = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a} - \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)\right\rangle_a
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-neutral pressure, $0$ denotes the neutral population, $a$ labels an internal state, $\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal neutral species in that state, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_a$ denotes averaging over internal states. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, which must be nonzero to define this projection.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and excludes thermal neutrals, ionized particles, and contributions from other species. When multiple internal states are present, their perpendicular pressures are averaged rather than summed; the averaging weights are unspecified. The [state-resolved perpendicular suprathermal neutral pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) instead applies to one specified internal state.

The transverse projection corresponds to the perpendicular component of [fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure), but the internal-state average defined here differs from that parent's internal-state-summed aggregation. Its directional counterpart is the [parallel fast neutral pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure), which resolves stress along the local magnetic field rather than across it.

items.name: tilt_angle_of_ferritic_element
items.description: Signed inclination of the second side of a parallelogram-shaped oblique cross-section of a ferritic element, measured counterclockwise from vertically upward +Z toward decreasing R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Signed inclination of the second side of a parallelogram-shaped oblique cross-section of a ferritic element is the $\beta$ orientation angle of that side in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is measured from the vertically upward $+Z$ direction.

Let $\mathbf{t}_\beta$ be the directed vector along the second side, with radial component $\Delta R_\beta$ along $\hat{R}$ and vertical component $\Delta Z_\beta$ along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The angle is defined by:

$$
\beta = \operatorname{atan2}(-\Delta R_\beta, \Delta Z_\beta)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ selects the signed quadrant of the directed side vector.

This quantity specifies orientation only. The first-side $\alpha$ inclination is the inclination angle of a ferritic element, the length of the $\alpha$ side is the [major length of a ferritic element](name:major_length_of_ferritic_element), and the length of the $\beta$ side is the minor length of a ferritic element. When the first-side and second-side inclinations are both zero, the parallelogram-shaped oblique cross-section reduces to the rectangular limiting geometry.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed second-side vector is rotated counterclockwise from the $+Z$ direction toward decreasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: density_at_divertor_target
items.description: Local number density of a specified plasma species or species group immediately upstream of a divertor-target sheath, with ion charge states summed and neutral populations excluded unless explicitly named.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local particle count per volume for a selected plasma species or species group at the plasma-facing side of a divertor target. It is evaluated immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath, rather than in the target material or as a quantity integrated over a target surface.

For a selected set of constituent populations, the number density is defined by:

$$
n_S = \sum_{s \in S} n_s
$$

where $n_S$ is the number density of the selected species or species group, $S$ is the set of included constituent populations, and $n_s$ is the number density of constituent population $s$.

The selected population can be free electrons, one ion species, or a named group of ion species such as deuterium and tritium. For an ion species, $S$ contains its positive atomic charge states and the sum is an unweighted particle-count sum; for a compound fuel group, it contains the included isotope ions. Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded unless explicitly named as part of $S$. The quantity is local to the plasma immediately upstream of one divertor-target sheath and is neither a target-surface integral nor an aggregation over multiple targets.

Species-specific instances refine this common definition, including [electron density at the divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), [boron density at the divertor target](name:boron_density_at_divertor_target), and [deuterium-tritium density at the divertor target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target). In contrast, [total ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) sums all charged ion species at a plasma boundary, making it broader in species scope and distinct in locus.

items.name: area_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting cross section of one poloidal-field-coil element in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle φ of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting cross section of one poloidal-field-coil element is the surface measure of the conductor region enclosed by that element boundary. It is defined in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an arbitrary conductor cross-section, the area is the integral of the differential surface measure over the conductor region $\mathcal{S}$:

$$
A = \int_{\mathcal{S}} dS
$$

where $A$ is the area of the poloidal-field-coil element, $\mathcal{S}$ is the conductor region in the poloidal plane, and $dS$ is the differential surface measure on that plane.

The quantity is per coil element, not a sum over multiple elements or over a complete coil. For a rectangular cross-section aligned with the $R$ and $Z$ directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $A = W H$, where $W$ is [width_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:width_of_poloidal_field_coil) and $H$ is [height_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:height_of_poloidal_field_coil); [thickness_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:thickness_of_poloidal_field_coil) is a separate geometric extent and is not the radial width in this relationship. For an annular cross-section, $A = \pi(r_\mathrm{out}^2-r_\mathrm{in}^2)$, where $r_\mathrm{out}$ is [outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) and $r_\mathrm{in}$ is [inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil). An insulation envelope, winding-pack envelope, or effective conducting area is a distinct quantity unless it is defined by the same boundary as $\mathcal{S}$.

items.name: krypton_prefill_count
items.description: Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 36 count units per atom.
items.documentation:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton (Kr) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral krypton atom contributes 36 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected krypton atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the krypton atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt = 36 \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless accumulated neutral-krypton atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the dimensionless atomic number of krypton, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the neutral-krypton atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only krypton introduced before breakdown and excludes later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with xenon_prefill_count providing the analogous noble-gas convention for xenon.

items.name: total_fast_ion_pressure
items.description: Gyrotropic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population summed over all charge states, characterized by independent components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The total fast-ion pressure represents the full gyrotropic kinetic stress of the suprathermal ion population, summed over all charge states, as a contribution to the plasma pressure balance. Fast ions — including fusion-born alpha particles, neutral-beam-injected ions, and radio-frequency-accelerated ions — retain pressure anisotropy with $P_\parallel \neq P_\perp$ relative to the local magnetic field because their pitch-angle scattering rate is slow compared with their energy transfer rate to the bulk plasma. The anisotropic structure is fully captured by the two independent scalar components [parallel total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

For a gyrotropic fast-ion distribution, the pressure tensor is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{P}_\text{fast} = P_{\perp}\,\overleftrightarrow{I} + (P_{\parallel} - P_{\perp})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel}$ and $P_{\perp}$ are the parallel and perpendicular scalar pressure components, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the identity tensor.

Fast-ion pressure profiles are obtained from kinetic particle-following or Fokker-Planck solvers that evolve the suprathermal distribution function under collisional slowing-down and pitch-angle scattering. The anisotropic fast-ion stress enters the MHD force balance and can drive pressure-anisotropy-driven instabilities when $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$ departs significantly from unity. The parent quantity [fast_ion_pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure) provides per-charge-state resolution.

In high-performance discharges with strong neutral beam or ion cyclotron resonance heating, fast-ion pressure can reach 10–50% of the total plasma pressure in the core, with anisotropy ratios $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$ ranging from near unity for isotropized distributions to several for strongly beam-like distributions.

items.name: boron_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the boron ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local boron-ion count per physical volume, summed over all boron ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the boron ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local boron-ion count per physical volume at that location. It represents boron ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutrals, or another plasma population, and is summed over all boron ionic charge states.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{B,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B,axis}}$ is the boron ion number density at the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of boron ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete ionized boron population at that location and excludes neutral boron; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density for another species.

This is the boron-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the same locus and aggregation convention as [beryllium density at the magnetic axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), but represents boron ions rather than beryllium ions. It differs from [boron density at the internal transport barrier](name:boron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is evaluated at a different plasma location.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description: Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the in-phase radial component of the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation for one toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction is the R component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the real part of the cylindrical radial component of a complex first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation for a selected toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction is the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining component is

$$
\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right)
$$

where $\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}}$ is this real component, $\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n$ is the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation for toroidal Fourier mode number $n$, $\operatorname{Re}$ takes the real part, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial basis vector.

Together with [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), it determines the complex [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field); changing the chosen complex phase of the harmonic rotates the real and imaginary parts without changing the represented perturbation. It is the radial component counterpart of [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and is distinct from a flux-surface-normal projection, which would use a unit normal to a specified flux coordinate rather than $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$.

Sign convention: Positive when the in-phase radial perturbation component points in the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall
items.description: Incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state as they arrive at a plasma-facing wall.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state as they cross onto a plasma-facing wall. It includes only translational kinetic energy and only particles moving from the plasma toward the wall.

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\left(-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

Here $q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy flux density, $s$ identifies the internal quantum state, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity relative to the wall, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ is the unit normal directed from the wall toward the plasma, and $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that state. Unlike [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall), this quantity weights arrivals by translational kinetic energy; neutral_energy_flux_at_wall aggregates the corresponding kinetic-energy flux over internal states. Internal excitation, potential, and rest-mass energies are excluded.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_power_density
items.description: Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by fast, suprathermal electrons for each toroidal mode number, resolved across a poloidal cross-section or represented as a flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave power density is the rate at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed by fast, suprathermal electrons per unit physical volume for each toroidal mode number.

For a toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local mode-resolved power density is defined as

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)} = \frac{dP_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the mode-resolved fast-electron power density, $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding [mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power), $V$ is physical volume, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and the subscripts $e$ and $\mathrm{fast}$ identify the fast-electron recipient population.

The recipient population is fast, suprathermal electrons; thermal-electron and ion absorption are distinct contributions. The quantity is specified separately for each toroidal mode number and may be given locally across a poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average over a magnetic flux surface.

This is a volumetric absorption rate, not volume-integrated power or launched wave power. The toroidal mode number identifies the wave harmonic contributing to absorption, not a Fourier coefficient of the deposited-power field.

Summing the mode contributions for the same spatial evaluation gives the [fast-electron absorbed wave power density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). Integrating a mode-resolved density over physical volume gives its corresponding mode-resolved absorbed wave power. Fast-electron absorption is one recipient contribution to the [mode-resolved total absorbed wave power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), which includes other plasma populations.

items.name: density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Local particle concentration of a specified plasma population at the magnetic axis, with ion charge states aggregated and compound fuel mixtures treated as defined populations.
items.documentation:
Particle number density at the magnetic axis is the local number of particles of a specified plasma population per physical volume at the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The quantity is population-specific and does not denote an unrestricted sum over all plasma species.

It is defined locally by:

$$
n_P(\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis}) = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{N_P(\Delta V;\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis})}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_P$ is the particle number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis}$ is the location of the magnetic axis, $N_P(\Delta V;\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis})$ is the number of particles from population $P$ within a physical volume $\Delta V$ centered at that location, and $\Delta V$ is the shrinking volume used to define the local limit.

The value is evaluated at the magnetic axis, rather than over a flux surface, plasma region, or volume, so it is not an average. For an ion species, the population count is summed over all positive ionic charge states and excludes neutral atoms; for electrons, it counts electrons directly. When the population is deuterium–tritium, the mixture is treated as one effective fuel population and includes the ionic charge states of both isotopes. These conventions distinguish particle number density from mass density, charge density, and the density of a single resolved charge state.

Species-specific instances include [argon density at the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), [electron density at the magnetic axis](name:electron_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [deuterium–tritium density at the magnetic axis](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis). The same population-specific density concept at another geometric locus is represented by [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) and [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier); those quantities differ in their evaluation location.

items.name: normal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description: Signed normal projection of the external-coil vacuum magnetic field with its toroidally averaged component removed, evaluated on a generic control surface.
items.documentation:
Normal non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the signed component of the toroidally varying external-coil vacuum magnetic field normal to a generic control surface. It is a scalar projection evaluated at points on that surface, rather than the full magnetic-field vector.

The defining projection is

$$
B_n(R,\phi,Z)=\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}(R,\phi,Z)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $B_n$ is the normal magnetic-field component, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is the [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented unit normal to the control surface. The coordinates $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are major radius, toroidal angle, and vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the external-coil vacuum contribution at each selected point of a generic control surface, which is not assumed to be a magnetic flux surface. Its aggregation convention is the inherited removal of the toroidal-angle average from the vacuum field; no surface or area average is implied.

It excludes the toroidally symmetric vacuum field and magnetic-field contributions generated by plasma currents. It also excludes tangential components and is distinct from cylindrical projections such as the [vertical non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field); the normal direction is defined by the control surface rather than by the cylindrical basis.

The scalar $B_n$ is the surface-normal component of the vector [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field). Reversing the assigned orientation of the control-surface normal reverses $B_n$, while the parent vector itself is unchanged.

Sign convention: Positive when the non-axisymmetric magnetic field points in the direction of the chosen positive unit normal to the control surface.

items.name: major_length_of_iron_core_segment
items.description: Euclidean length of the alpha-side of an iron-core segment’s oblique parallelogram cross-section in a constant-toroidal-angle poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The side is inclined relative to the major-radius direction and the value is a non-negative distance.
items.documentation:
Euclidean length of the alpha-side of an iron-core segment’s oblique parallelogram cross-section is the non-negative distance between the two endpoints of that designated side. The edge lies in a constant-$\phi$ poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; its inclination is specified by [alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment](name:alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment).

For endpoints 1 and 2 of the designated alpha-side, the length is

$$
L_\alpha = \sqrt{(R_2 - R_1)^2 + (Z_2 - Z_1)^2}
$$

where $L_\alpha$ is this alpha-side length, and $R_i$ and $Z_i$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of endpoint $i$.

The quantity is the alpha-side specialization of [length_of_iron_core_segment](name:minor_length_of_iron_core_segment). It excludes the other parallelogram side, the full cross-sectional extent, and [height_of_iron_core_segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), which denotes a different iron-core segment dimension. Because it is a Euclidean length, it is not a signed orientation, coordinate displacement, or vector projection.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source per unit volume from the magnetic force on counter-passing particles' current across magnetic flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density delivered to counter-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with their current across magnetic flux surfaces. Toroidal angular momentum is angular momentum about the symmetry axis; its source is a [torque density](name:torque_density), not a toroidal force density.

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}} = \left\langle R\,\left(j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}\hat{\mathbf n}\times\mathbf B\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is this torque density, $j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is the signed conventional current density carried across magnetic flux surfaces by counter-passing particles, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the unit normal toward increasing flux-surface label $\psi$, and $\mathbf B$ is the magnetic field. The brackets denote a normalized average over the surface labeled by $\psi$. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, and $\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}$ points toward increasing $\phi$. The moment arm $R$ remains inside the average.

Counter-passing particles occupy nontrapped passing orbits whose circulation along the magnetic field opposes the plasma-current direction. Only the counter-passing part of the specified particle species' distribution contributes; co-passing and trapped particles and other torque mechanisms are excluded. This is a flux-surface average, not an unaveraged local source or a volume-integrated torque.

This quantity is the toroidal angular-momentum source component of the [counter-passing Lorentz-force torque density](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force). The [co-passing counterpart](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) applies the same mechanism to co-passing particles. It is distinct from the [thermal-plasma return-current torque](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), which acts on thermal plasma through compensating currents.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic force supplies toroidal angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: boron_density_at_limiter
items.description: Boron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral boron atoms.
items.documentation:
Boron density at a limiter is the local number density of boron ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}=\sum_{q=1}^{5}n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of counted boron ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the density of boron charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The sum includes boron ions from B$^{+}$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ and excludes neutral boron atoms. This is the boron-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter); unlike [boron density at the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is evaluated specifically at the limiter-side location.

items.name: total_co_passing_particle_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on untrapped orbits circulating with the plasma current, including thermal and nonthermal particles; the corresponding local density is defined at each point before averaging over its magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Total co-passing particle density is the number density contributed by particles of a selected species whose untrapped guiding-center orbits circulate in the direction of the plasma current. It includes thermal and nonthermal particles and may be specified locally or as a flux-surface average.

The local density is the velocity-space integral over this orbit class, and its flux-surface average is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) &= \int_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \\
\bar n_{s,\mathrm{co}} &= \left\langle n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is the local co-passing number density, $\bar n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is its flux-surface average, and $s$ labels the selected species. The distribution function of species $s$ is $f_s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element; and $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space region associated with untrapped orbits circulating with the plasma current. The brackets denote a normalized average over the magnetic flux surface through $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathrm{FS}$ denotes that surface.

The local form applies at a spatial point, while the averaged form applies over the magnetic flux surface through that point; the averaged form is not a local point value. Thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected species contribute additively, and the quantity is not summed over different species. It excludes the [total counter-passing particle density](name:total_counter_passing_particle_density) and [total trapped particle density](name:total_trapped_particle_density), which describe distinct orbit classes.

At matching local or flux-surface-averaged scope, [co-passing fast-particle density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) is the suprathermal contribution included here. This co-passing orbit-class contribution is part of [particle density](name:particle_density), which also includes other particle populations.

items.name: perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged transverse kinetic stress of nonthermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma current.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure is the flux-surface-averaged field-perpendicular component of the kinetic stress of a represented nonthermal particle species. Co-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits with orbit-averaged toroidal motion in the plasma-current direction.

The component is defined by the transverse second moment of the co-passing fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\int_{\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})}\frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the represented species, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset belonging to co-passing orbits at that position, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The squared transverse speed is $v_\perp^2=|\mathbf{v}-(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$, where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The factor of one-half gives the mean stress in the two field-perpendicular directions.

The brackets denote a normalized magnetic-flux-surface average with weight proportional to $dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $dS$ is the surface-area element and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label. Thus the quantity is a surface average, not a local stress at one point.

Only the co-passing nonthermal population contributes; thermal, trapped, and counter-passing particles are excluded. Multiple fast-particle populations of the represented species contribute additively, not through a density-weighted mean; no all-species or all-charge-state total is implied. Particle velocities are used without subtracting the mean flow, so perpendicular directed-motion stress is retained.

Together with the [parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), this component determines the [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) through $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}=(p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}+2p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}})/3$, where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace and $p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the corresponding field-parallel component, with the same population restriction and flux-surface averaging.

items.name: length_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description: Total physical arclength of the optical fiber centerline in a fiber-optic current sensor, defining its optical propagation distance and distributed magneto-optic interaction length.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total arclength of the optical fiber centerline forming the fiber-optic current sensor. It includes the complete winding path and is not the straight-line distance between endpoints or the length of the sensor outline.

For a centerline parameterized by an arbitrary parameter $u$, the fiber length is defined by

$$
L = \int_{u_0}^{u_1} \left|\frac{d\mathbf{r}}{du}\right|\,du
$$

where $L$ is the total fiber arclength, $\mathbf{r}(u)$ is the centerline position, and $u_0$ and $u_1$ delimit the fiber path. The length sets the optical propagation distance; accumulated Faraday rotation additionally depends on the magnetic-field projection along the winding and the [Verdet constant](name:verdet_constant_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor).

items.name: line_averaged_oxygen_density
items.description: Line-averaged oxygen density is the line-of-sight mean of the local oxygen number density, summed over all charge states from neutral O0 through fully stripped O8+, along a specified chord through the plasma.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged oxygen density is the line-of-sight mean of the local oxygen number density—summed over all charge states from neutral O$^0$ through fully stripped O$^{8+}$—along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the oxygen impurity concentration averaged by arclength rather than the value at a single point.

For a chord of length $L$, the line-averaged oxygen density is defined by:

$$
\bar{n}_\mathrm{O} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_\mathrm{O}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\bar{n}_\mathrm{O}$ is the line-averaged oxygen density, $L$ is the physical length of the chord segment included in the average, $\ell$ is arclength along that chord, and $n_\mathrm{O}(\ell)$ is the [local oxygen density](name:oxygen_density) at the point labeled by $\ell$.

The scope is the species-level oxygen impurity population intersected by the specified chord: the density is charge-state-summed over neutral oxygen and all oxygen ions, and the spatial aggregation is an arclength average along the chord. It excludes charge-state-resolved oxygen densities, the local point value [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), and the spatial mean over the confined plasma volume.

The essential relationship to [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density) is that the local charge-state-summed density is the integrand of the chord average. [Volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) is the analogous mean formed over a plasma volume, whereas this quantity is formed only along the specified line of sight and is normalized by the chord length.

items.name: power_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volume-integrated net power transferred to a plasma particle population through Coulomb collisions, abstracting over all source and receiving population combinations without prescribing which species serve as donor or receiver.
items.documentation:
Coulomb collisions mediate energy exchange between plasma populations — electrons, thermal ions, fast particles, impurity ions, and neutrals — converting differential kinetic energy into thermal energy of the receiving species. This abstract parent captures the general concept of volume-integrated collisional power transfer without specifying which populations participate; every concrete child quantity carries explicit population labels to identify the donor and receiver.

The volume-integrated collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll}$ is the local collisional power exchange density and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

Concrete population-resolved instances of this quantity include [ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which covers the total ion population summed over all species and charge states, and ion_state_power_due_to_collisions, which resolves this to a specified ionization state. Source-resolved variants such as [fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions), and [thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) additionally identify the donating population.

Sign convention: Positive when net energy is deposited into the specified receiving population (net collisional heating); negative when the receiving population loses energy to others (net collisional cooling).

items.name: first_local_tangential_radius_of_filter_window
items.description: Geometric radius describing the bending of an X-ray filter window along its first local tangential direction, defined for applicable curved-surface geometries.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local radius describing how an X-ray filter-window surface bends along its first local tangential direction.

For the surface normal section tangent to that direction, the curvature radius is defined by:

$$
R = \frac{1}{|\kappa_1|}
$$

where $R$ is the first-local-tangential radius of curvature and $\kappa_1$ is the normal curvature along the first local tangent.

This quantity applies to an individual filter window when its curved-surface geometry specifies bending along the first local tangent. It describes surface shape, not aperture size, and is a radius rather than curvature itself. No front/back surface distinction is implied.

This is a directional surface-curvature specialization of [radius](name:radius). The [second-local-tangential radius](name:second_local_tangential_radius_of_filter_window) describes bending along the other local tangent; neither tangent is necessarily a principal-curvature direction.

items.name: tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament
items.description: Signed beta inclination of the beta-angle side of a plasma-filament parallelogram cross-section in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured counterclockwise from +Z toward decreasing R.
items.documentation:
The tilt angle of a plasma filament is the signed inclination $\beta$ of the beta-angle side of a plasma-filament parallelogram cross-section. The angle lies in the poloidal $(R,Z)$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height, and is referenced to the upward $+Z$ direction.

For the ordered parallelogram, let $\mathbf{u}_\beta = u_R\hat{R}+u_Z\hat{Z}$ be the unit vector along the beta-angle side, directed from the reference vertex shared with the base side toward the adjacent beta-side vertex. The signed angle is defined by:

$$
\beta = \operatorname{atan2}(-u_R, u_Z)
$$

where $u_R$ and $u_Z$ are the components of $\mathbf{u}_\beta$ along $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the principal branch $-\pi < \beta \le \pi$.

The beta-angle side terminology follows the same angle-labeled parallelogram convention as [length of iron-core segment](name:minor_length_of_iron_core_segment), identifying a side by its inclination angle rather than by an ordinal label. The directed-edge and branch conventions make $\beta$ unique: translating to the opposite parallel edge leaves the value unchanged, while reversing the side direction is excluded. This angle complements cross-section size quantities such as [plasma-filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) and thickness of plasma filament; it is not a filament-current direction or a magnetic-field pitch angle.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed beta-angle side is rotated counterclockwise from the upward $+Z$ direction in the poloidal $(R,Z)$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, drawn with $R$ increasing to the right.

items.name: temperature_at_divertor_target
items.description: Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a divertor-target sheath. It refers to the sheath-entrance plasma population, not to the solid target material or to an average over different populations.
items.documentation:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a divertor-target sheath. It characterizes the random kinetic part of the particle distribution at the sheath entrance, the boundary at which sheath-entry conditions such as the Bohm criterion are posed, and is not a thermodynamic property of the solid target material.

For a population $s$, the scalar target temperature is the one-third trace of the kinetic thermal-energy moment over the velocity-space domain of that population at the sheath entrance:

$$
T_{s,t} = \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,t}} |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t}|^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{s,t}$ is the temperature at the divertor target for population $s$, subscript $t$ denotes the divertor-target sheath entrance, $m_s$ is the particle mass of population $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is the number density of that population at the sheath entrance, $\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ is the full velocity-space domain of the specified sheath-entrance population, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow velocity of the population at the sheath entrance, $f_{s,t}$ is its velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The distribution normalization is such that integrating $f_{s,t}$ over $\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ gives $n_{s,t}$.

The specified population can be an electron population, an ion population, a charge state, or another plasma population identified separately. If a species is represented without charge-state resolution, this intensive value is the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The unqualified quantity does not imply an average over different plasma populations or over positions on the divertor target.

For the electron population it corresponds to the [electron temperature at divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), and for the ion population it corresponds to the [ion temperature at divertor target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is the divertor-target specialization of the more general [plasma temperature](name:plasma_temperature). The moment definition makes it two thirds of the population-averaged random kinetic energy at the sheath entrance, not the full mean random kinetic energy per particle.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon ions at the magnetic axis, averaged over all neon ionization states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion bulk velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean over all neon ionization states and excludes neutral neon.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-aggregated neon-ion bulk velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The magnetic axis is the point inside the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes, $\nabla\psi=0$. The analogous quantity at the plasma boundary is [toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_wave_electric_field
items.description: Complex phasor of the wave electric field projected along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
The parallel wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It retains both amplitude and phase and is a component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field).

The parallel component is defined by

$$
E_{\parallel}=\mathbf{E}_{w}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_{0}}{|\mathbf{B}_{0}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}_{w}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{B}_{0}$ is the local equilibrium magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction. The phasor carries the phase of the harmonic field under the selected time convention.

This quantity is the complex component rather than its magnitude. Its modulus gives the parallel wave electric field amplitude, while its quadratures include the [parallel wave electric field imaginary part](name:parallel_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part) and the corresponding real part.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field component is directed along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description: Outgoing recombination energy flux at the wall is the emitted energy per unit area and time attributable to a specified incident-ion species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the outgoing energy transfer associated with surface recombination of a specified incident-ion species and charge state. The charge-state label identifies the incident ion responsible for recombination, not the charge state of an emitted product.

The local emitted energy flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}}{\partial A\,\partial t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the outgoing recombination energy flux attributable to incident-ion species $s$ and charge state $Z$, $W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the corresponding cumulative emitted recombination-associated energy, $A$ is wall area, and $t$ is time. The superscripts $\mathrm{em}$ and $\mathrm{rec}$ denote emission and recombination, respectively.

The quantity applies locally at the wall, with incident-ion species and charge state held fixed. Recombination channels and emitted product species and states are summed; incident-ion species and charge states are not. It is an energy flux per unit area, not a wall-integrated power, and excludes energy transferred through non-recombination channels.

Summing over incident-ion species and charge states gives the [ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), the ion-associated contribution to the broader [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). Unlike the [incident-ion recombination energy flux](name:incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this quantity describes energy emitted from the wall rather than energy delivered to it. It is neither incoming kinetic-energy flux nor an incident-minus-emitted net balance.

items.name: total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description: Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma and including both the toroidal projection of the thermal-ion contribution and the summed fast-ion contributions from angular-momentum exchange with co-existing species.
items.documentation:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state is the signed toroidal collisional angular-momentum source for that charge state, integrated over the plasma. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total torque is the additive thermal-plus-fast scalar contribution:

$$
\tau^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
=
\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
+
\sum_f \tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies the charge state, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), $\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its axial projection associated with toroidal angular momentum, $f$ indexes fast-ion sub-populations, and $\tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [toroidal fast ion charge-state collisional torque](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) for sub-population $f$.

Only torque due to Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with co-existing charged plasma species is included. This quantity is charge-state resolved, not summed over charge states, and is distinct from the corresponding local total ion charge-state collisional torque density.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions transfer toroidal angular momentum to the specified ion charge state in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: effective_particle_energy
items.description: Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic kinetic-energy-like coordinate that orders a species in velocity space and may be scaled by a positive reference energy.
items.documentation:
Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic velocity-space energy assigned to a particle species through a kinetic-energy-like weight. It provides the energy coordinate used to order that species in velocity space and is the unnormalized concept underlying [normalized effective particle energy](name:normalized_effective_particle_energy). It differs from [particle energy](name:particle_energy), which denotes the energy content of the full distribution.

The effective energy is defined by the selected velocity-space weight:

$$
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}(\boldsymbol{\xi}) = w_s(\boldsymbol{\xi})
$$

where $s$ labels the species, $\boldsymbol{\xi}$ denotes its velocity-space variables, and $w_s$ is a kinetic-energy-like weight, such as the total kinetic energy or a directional component. A normalized specialization divides $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}$ by a strictly positive species reference energy. This quantity is distinct from perturbed particle energy, which describes a moment of a distribution perturbation rather than the effective energy coordinate itself.

items.name: reference_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description: Reference wavelength of a spectrometer channel is the absolute vacuum wavelength at the center of its spectral instrument function; a bin-specific value refers to the center of that detector bin's response.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of spectrometer channel

The reference wavelength is the absolute vacuum wavelength at the center of the channel's spectral instrument function. It is a response-position wavelength, distinct from the wavelength of a spectral line or a wavelength selected as a calibration reference.

The response-center wavelength is defined by

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}} = \operatorname{center}_{\lambda}\!\left[\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\lambda)\right]
$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference wavelength, $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\lambda)$ is the channel's spectral instrument function as a function of $\lambda$, $\lambda$ is [vacuum wavelength], and $\operatorname{center}_{\lambda}$ denotes the wavelength coordinate at the center of the response function.

The value applies to the channel response or, when specified for a vertical detector bin, that bin's response; it is not an average across bins. The response spread about this center is characterized separately by the [width of a spectrometer channel](name:width_of_spectrometer_channel). The [reference calibration wavelength of a spectrometer channel](name:reference_calibration_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel) is distinct: it is the zero-pixel intercept of a linear pixel-to-vacuum-wavelength relation.

items.name: temperature_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Energy-equivalent temperature scale at the magnetic axis, representing either particle thermal energy or radiation brightness.
items.documentation:
Temperature at the magnetic axis is an energy-equivalent measure of a thermal state or radiation field evaluated at the magnetic axis. It provides a shared parent concept for kinetic temperatures and brightness temperatures, which need not represent the same underlying physical state.

For a temperature parameter expressed as an energy-equivalent quantity, the defining conversion is:

$$
\Theta = k_{\mathrm B} T
$$

where $\Theta$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $T$ is the underlying thermodynamic or brightness-temperature parameter, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is Boltzmann's constant. This conversion does not imply that a radiation brightness temperature equals the local kinetic temperature.

The quantity is evaluated at the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The parent name specifies no particle species, charge-state aggregation, radiation band, or population-weighting convention; it is therefore neither a charge-state sum nor an all-plasma aggregate by itself.

The [electron temperature at the magnetic axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the kinetic-temperature specialization for electrons. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the brightness-temperature specialization for electron-cyclotron radiation and is not necessarily the local kinetic electron temperature. Unlike [plasma temperature](name:plasma_temperature), this parent does not require an effective fluid or magnetohydrodynamic aggregation.

items.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal reference location, projected along the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal oxygen velocity at the pedestal top characterizes the impurity ion fluid flow projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction at the H-mode edge transport barrier's outer shoulder, where the steep-gradient pedestal region transitions to the flatter core profile. Oxygen (atomic number $Z = 8$) is a common intrinsic or deliberately seeded impurity in tokamaks, present in charge states spanning O$^{5+}$ through O$^{8+}$ in the pedestal; this quantity represents the oxygen fluid velocity aggregated over the predominant charge states unless a specific ionization state is separately resolved.

The toroidal component is defined by the projection:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen ion fluid velocity vector evaluated at the pedestal-top locus.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, which resolves the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines following charge exchange with an injected neutral beam. Toroidal rotation velocities at the pedestal top in H-mode span roughly $10^3$–$10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, reflecting neutral beam torque input, intrinsic rotation, and impurity-specific flow corrections. Comparison with [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) enables cross-species benchmarking of pedestal rotation profiles.

Sign convention: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density
items.description: Temporal standard deviation of the total ion charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at a plasma-facing probe.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temporal standard deviation of the total ion-carried charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at the specified plasma-facing probe. Ion contributions from all included species and charge states are summed with their signed charge weighting before the fluctuation statistic is evaluated. It is the parallel specialization of [fluctuating ion current density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density).

With $t$ denoting time in seconds, the defining relation is:

$$
\sigma_{j_i,\parallel}=\left\langle\left[j_{i,\parallel}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\parallel}\right\rangle_t\right]^2\right\rangle_t^{1/2},\qquad j_{i,\parallel}(t)=\mathbf{j}_i(t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(t),\qquad \hat{\mathbf b}(t)=\frac{\mathbf{B}(t)}{|\mathbf{B}(t)|}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_i$ is the aggregated ion current-density vector in A m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field in tesla, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes the temporal average.

The aggregation and projection precede the standard-deviation operation; this is not a sum of separately calculated species fluctuations. Unlike [fluctuating saturated ion current density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density), it represents the total ion current rather than only the ion-saturation current component. The result is nonnegative even when the underlying parallel current changes sign.

items.name: deuterium_prefill_count
items.description: Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with one count unit per atom.
items.documentation:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium (D) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral deuterium atom contributes one equivalent electron.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected deuterium atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the deuterium atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-deuterium atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the deuterium atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the deuterium atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only deuterium introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterium-specific component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count) and uses the same isotope-resolved convention as tritium_prefill_count.

items.name: accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms introduced by gas injection during plasma prefill before plasma breakdown, with two count units assigned per atom.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the cumulative inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It covers injection before plasma breakdown and excludes helium-3 introduced after breakdown.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} = 2\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injected helium-3 atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s.

This is the pre-breakdown counterpart of [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection); [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) represents the instantaneous rate rather than the accumulated inventory.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_filter_window
items.description: First local tangential width of the filter window is its full rectangular-aperture extent along the object-local first tangential axis.
items.documentation:
Width of filter window

For rectangular geometry, the full width is the difference between the greatest and least boundary coordinates along that axis:

$$
w = \xi_{1,\max} - \xi_{1,\min}
$$

where $w$ is the first local tangential width, and $\xi_{1,\max}$ and $\xi_{1,\min}$ are the greatest and least values, respectively, of the [first local tangential coordinate of the filter window](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_filter_window) on the aperture boundary.

This quantity applies to one filter window only when its geometry is rectangular. It is a full width, not a half-width or a signed boundary coordinate, and is distinct from the [filter-window radius](name:radius_of_filter_window), which describes the opening for circular geometry.

Together with the [second local tangential width of the filter window](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_filter_window), it specifies the two orthogonal dimensions of the rectangular aperture.

items.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
items.description: Dimensionless vector of normalized energy-weighted velocity-space moments of a species' perturbed particle distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized particle energy moment of a species' perturbed velocity distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its components use distinct squared velocity-direction weights while sharing an energy-weighted normalization from the corresponding unperturbed species distribution.

For species $s$ and selected velocity direction or weighting component $a$, the normalized moment is defined by

$$
\mathcal{E}_{a,s} = \frac{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v_a^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v^4 f_{0s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v$ is its magnitude, $v_a$ is the selected velocity component, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution, $f_{0s}$ is the unperturbed distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity is a particle moment, distinct from gyrocenter moments and from unweighted density or pressure moments. The [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) is its perpendicular directional realization.

items.name: neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
items.description: Global neutron production rate from thermonuclear reactions among Maxwellian bulk ions, applicable to individual neutron-producing reaction channels or their aggregate total, excluding fast-ion fusion contributions.
items.documentation:
The neutron source rate due to thermal fusion is the global rate at which neutrons are generated by thermonuclear reactions between plasma ion species whose velocity distributions are Maxwellian. It encompasses both per-channel rates for a single neutron-producing reaction (DD, DT, or TT) and the aggregate sum over all channels, and is an instance of the general [source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion) restricted to the neutron product.

For each neutron-producing reaction channel $c$ between reactant species $a$ and $b$, the channel source rate is:

$$
S_{n,c}^{\rm th} = \frac{1}{1 + \delta_{ab}} \int n_a \, n_b \, \langle \sigma v \rangle_c \, dV
$$

where $n_a$ and $n_b$ are the number densities of the two reactant species, $\langle \sigma v \rangle_c$ is the Maxwell-averaged reaction-rate coefficient for channel $c$, $\delta_{ab} = 1$ when the two reactants are identical (as in DD and TT channels) and 0 otherwise, and the integral extends over the confined plasma volume. The aggregate quantity sums contributions from all neutron-producing channels.

This quantity excludes neutrons from beam-target fusion (see flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion), beam-beam fusion, fusion-product reactivation, and radio-frequency-tail ion populations. Per-channel instances include deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion and tritium_tritium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion; the channel-summed total is [total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_plasma_filament
items.description: Radial coordinate of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the oblique reference point anchoring one current-carrying filament element's rectangular cross-section.
items.documentation:
Radial coordinate of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate of the oblique reference point that anchors one current-carrying plasma filament element's rectangular cross-section. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to a single plasma filament element represented by oblique rectangular cross-sectional geometry. It is the coordinate of the reference point used by that representation, not the filament width, height, centroid position, magnetic-axis position, or a flux-surface radial coordinate; no averaging or summation over filament elements is implied.

Together with the vertical coordinate of the plasma filament, it locates the oblique reference point in the poloidal plane. The [alpha angle of the plasma filament](name:alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament) and beta angle of the plasma filament are defined relative to this same reference point, and the [plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) is a rectangular cross-section extent anchored by it.

items.name: ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description: Cumulative wave power absorbed by all ion populations — thermal and fast — within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The ion power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which wave energy is deposited into the ion population — spanning both thermal bulk ions and fast (non-thermal) ions — within the plasma volume bounded by a closed magnetic flux surface. It is the ion-channel component of the more general [power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface), separating ion energy absorption from the corresponding electron heating contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the total ion wave-power density $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the flux surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_i(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_i(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_i$ is the ion volumetric heating power density in W m$^{-3}$ and $\psi$ is the chosen flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

The population-resolved breakdown is given by [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) for the bulk ion channel and [fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) for non-thermal beam or fusion-born ions. This cumulative radial profile enables power-balance analysis and is inferred from combining absorbed-power density profiles computed via wave ray-tracing or Monte Carlo beam-deposition codes with equilibrium flux-surface geometry.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part
items.description: Quadrature poloidal velocity component of a complex first-order plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic. It is the imaginary part of the projection onto the positive poloidal direction, paired with the in-phase real part.
items.documentation:
Quadrature poloidal velocity component of a complex first-order plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction is the imaginary part of the poloidal projection of that eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic. The poloidal direction is the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in a flux-coordinate basis $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\phi$ the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projected component and its imaginary part are defined by

$$
v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}} = \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\tilde v_\theta\right), \qquad \tilde v_\theta = \tilde{\mathbf v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta
$$

where $\tilde{\mathbf v}$ is the complex first-order plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction, $\tilde v_\theta$ is its poloidal component, and $v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}}$ is the coefficient of the imaginary term when $\tilde v_\theta = v_{\theta,\mathrm{re}} + i v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}}$.

This quantity is the quadrature component paired with the [poloidal perturbed plasma velocity real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part); together they specify the complex [poloidal perturbed plasma velocity](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity) for the chosen harmonic and phase convention. It is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal perturbed plasma velocity imaginary part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), which projects the same complex velocity perturbation onto the toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the quadrature component of $\tilde{\mathbf v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is aligned with $+\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$, toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate basis $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description: In-phase real coefficient of the toroidal magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum surrounding the plasma, resolved for one toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real part of the toroidal component of the first-order complex magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum surrounding the plasma. It is one component of the full [toroidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) and excludes the equilibrium field and perturbations within the plasma.

The real coefficient is defined from the complex toroidal perturbation by

$$
\delta B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta B_\phi\right], \qquad \delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the complex first-order perturbed magnetic-field vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\delta B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the quantity belongs to the specified toroidal Fourier mode; its quadrature counterpart is the [imaginary part of the toroidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). In the vacuum region, the perturbation is current-free and satisfies $\nabla \times \delta\mathbf{B}=0$.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal perturbation component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description: Measure of how rapidly a toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate changes in space, obtained from the magnitude of its spatial gradient.
items.documentation:
This quantity represents the local geometric rate at which a toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate changes through physical space. It is the magnitude-based measure derived from the spatial gradient, independent of any particular direction or projection.

The defining relation is

$$
\left|\nabla \chi\right| = \sqrt{\nabla\chi \cdot \nabla\chi}
$$

where $\chi$ is the toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate, $\nabla$ is the spatial-gradient operator, and the dot denotes the Euclidean inner product of the gradient with itself.

The local form is evaluated pointwise and is not intrinsically flux-surface averaged or squared. The [flux-surface-averaged toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude) applies a flux-surface average to this measure, while [square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude) applies the algebraic square. Both are derived from the underlying [toroidal flux coordinate gradient](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient), which retains the full spatial-gradient quantity rather than its magnitude.

items.name: parallel_runaway_electron_current_density
items.description: Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned component of conventional current density carried by runaway electrons.
items.documentation:
Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned contribution to conventional electric-current density carried by runaway electrons. It is the runaway-electron contribution to [parallel current density](name:parallel_current_density), not the total plasma current.

For a flux-surface-resolved value, the magnetic-field-weighted definition is:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{B_0}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the flux-surface-resolved parallel runaway-electron current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the current-density vector carried by runaway electrons, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field. The reference field is positive toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The contribution includes runaway electrons without restriction to a particular orbit class; currents carried by other particle populations are excluded. It is a signed scalar component, not the magnitude of the runaway-electron current-density vector, a toroidal projection, or total [current density](name:current_density).

At a point, the field-aligned component is the projection of the current-density vector onto the local magnetic-field direction, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. The flux-surface value above is not generally the unweighted flux-surface average of this pointwise component. [Volume-averaged parallel runaway-electron current density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density) instead uses a plasma-volume average.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged contraction $\langle\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ has the same sign as $B_0, with $B_0$ positive toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: hard_xray_emissivity
items.description: Local production rate of hard-X-ray bremsstrahlung photons per plasma volume and emission solid angle, integrated over a specified photon-energy band.
items.documentation:
Hard-X-ray emissivity is the local bremsstrahlung photon production rate per plasma volume and emission solid angle, integrated over the selected hard-X-ray photon-energy band. It represents emission from suprathermal electrons at a physical location and in a specified emission direction.

The band-integrated emissivity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}(\mathbf{r},\Omega;E_1,E_2)=\int_{E_1}^{E_2}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}^{(E)}(\mathbf{r},\Omega,E)\,\mathrm{d}E
$$

where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}$ is the band-integrated hard-X-ray photon emissivity, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}^{(E)}$ is the differential photon emissivity with respect to photon energy, $\mathbf{r}$ is the emission location, $\Omega$ is the emission direction labeled by solid angle, $E$ is photon energy, and $E_1$ and $E_2$ are the lower and upper limits of the selected energy band.

This quantity is local and directional: it is not integrated along a line of sight, over a plasma volume, or over emission directions. It applies to hard-X-ray photons produced by suprathermal-electron bremsstrahlung and excludes the total bremsstrahlung electromagnetic power and detector-received radiation.

In an optically thin plasma, [hard X-ray brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness) is obtained from the corresponding local emissivity by propagation and integration along a viewing path; brightness is therefore a received radiance, whereas this quantity is the local photon source density.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_source
items.description: Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral population. It includes charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions.
items.documentation:
