Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral population after normalization by the transport area. It represents the vector rate at which charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions add momentum to, or remove momentum from, that resolved neutral state.

The defining process decomposition is:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cx}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{ion}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{rec}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{el}}
$$

where \(\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)}\) is this momentum source for neutral species \(n\) in internal state \(\alpha\), and the terms on the right are the contributions from charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions, respectively.

The quantity is resolved for one neutral species and one internal state; it is not the state-summed [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), which is obtained by summing this vector over all resolved internal states of that neutral species. It is the neutral-state analog of the [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), with resolution by internal state rather than ion charge state. A directional component such as the [radial neutral-internal-state momentum source](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) is the projection of this vector onto the corresponding direction; `radial` denotes the \(\hat{R}\) component in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\).

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component represents momentum transferred to the neutral species in the resolved internal state along the positive basis direction used for that component; in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\), the radial, toroidal, and vertical components are positive along \(+\hat{R}\), increasing toroidal angle \(\phi\), and \(+\hat{Z}\), respectively.

items.name: opacity_at_ece_channel_emission_position
items.description: Dimensionless optical depth along the electron-cyclotron-emission viewing path at a channel emission position, indicating whether the detected emission is local and thermal.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the optical depth of the plasma evaluated at the emission position associated with one electron-cyclotron-emission channel. It measures the cumulative attenuation between the emitting region and the relevant observation path.

The optical depth is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s_{\mathrm{em}}) = \int_{\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})} \alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s)\,ds
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-emission optical depth, $s_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the channel emission position, $\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})$ is the line-of-sight path used to accumulate the optical depth at that position, $\alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-emission absorption coefficient, and $s$ is distance along that path.

The scope is one channel and its associated emission position; values are not summed or averaged over channels or over emission positions. This quantity is the accumulated optical depth, not the local absorption coefficient or a channel-integrated aggregate. It is the position-specific form of [opacity](name:opacity), with the evaluation locus made explicit.

Optical depth greater than one indicates optically thick, locally thermal emission, whereas optical depth less than one indicates that non-local or suprathermal contributions can be important.

items.name: accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative number of tritium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each tritium atom corresponds to one equivalent electron.
items.documentation:
The accumulated tritium count due to gas injection is the running total of tritium ($^3\mathrm{H}$) atoms introduced to the plasma vessel through gas injection valves, accumulated continuously from plasma breakdown onward. The quantity is dimensionless, representing each injected atom as an equivalent-electron contribution scaled by its atomic number.

For tritium, whose atomic number is $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron inventory equals the raw atom count directly:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z \cdot N_\mathrm{atoms} = N_\mathrm{atoms}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{atoms}$ is the total number of tritium atoms injected after breakdown. The equivalent-electron convention provides a species-independent basis for comparing injected particle inventories — for higher-$Z$ species such as argon ($Z = 18$), the multiplier is correspondingly larger.

This is the time-integrated form of tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection, accumulating monotonically as gas is puffed after breakdown. Tritium introduced before breakdown is tracked separately as tritium_prefill_count. The deuterium analog in the same equivalent-electron framework is [deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: height_of_passive_structure
items.description: Full vertical extent of a rectangular cross-section of a passive conducting structure element, measured parallel to Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The height is the full vertical extent of a rectangular cross-section of a passive conducting structure element, measured along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

It is defined by the difference between the upper and lower vertical coordinates:

$$
H = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $H$ is the full height, and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical coordinates of the upper and lower cross-section boundaries, respectively.

This quantity is the full height, not a half-height, local thickness, or horizontal width. Its corresponding horizontal dimension is the [full horizontal width of a passive conducting structure element](name:width_of_passive_structure).

items.name: reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description: Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the RF power returning toward the source through the transmission line because of impedance mismatch at the plasma–antenna interface.
items.documentation:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the nonnegative RF power propagating back toward the source because of impedance mismatch at the plasma–antenna interface. It is the returning-power component of the wave-power budget represented by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), evaluated at the module input reference plane.

The module power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward power](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) arriving at the module input reference plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the reflected power returning toward the source, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net [launched power](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) entering the vacuum vessel from that module. All three components refer to the same module and reference plane.

Reflected power is the portion of forward power returned toward the source, distinct from net launched power and power absorbed by the plasma. The quantity applies to one antenna module and is not a sum over modules or antennas.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged kinetic stress of suprathermal particles of one species per degree of freedom perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular fast-particle pressure is the flux-surface average of the field-perpendicular component of the gyrotropic kinetic stress carried by suprathermal particles of a specified species. It represents stress per transverse degree of freedom, rather than the sum of the two transverse stresses.

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second moment of the fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{2}\int v_\perp^2 f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of the velocity perpendicular to the local magnetic field, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The brackets denote a normalized flux-surface average with weight proportional to the reciprocal magnitude of the gradient of a smooth flux-surface label.

This quantity includes only the nonthermal population of the selected species. Multiple fast-particle populations of that same species are superposed in the distribution function and therefore contribute additively to the pressure. It is not a sum over distinct species, is not restricted to a single orbit class, and excludes the thermal-population pressure. Unlike the local perpendicular stress, it includes flux-surface averaging.

The corresponding [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), denoted by $p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$, is the independent field-aligned stress component. Together they determine the isotropic [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure), $p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$, through $p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}})/3$, with all three quantities referring to the same species, suprathermal population, and flux-surface average. The parallel and perpendicular components need not be equal.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Poloidal component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, represented as a linear MHD eigenfunction and distinct from its radial and toroidal components.
items.documentation:
The poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is the poloidal component of the first-order departure of the plasma magnetic vector potential from its reference state. In linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenfunction descriptions, it carries the poloidal part of the magnetic-vector-potential perturbation without selecting a real or imaginary phase component.

The perturbed magnetic field associated with the full vector potential perturbation satisfies

$$
\delta \mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \delta \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic field, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, and $\delta \mathbf{A}$ is the full perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential. The poloidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate.

This quantity is restricted to the poloidal component and is not the complete vector potential, its radial component, its toroidal component, or the perturbed magnetic field itself. It is also distinct from the real-valued specialization [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part), which selects one phase component of the corresponding eigenfunction.

The component is a specialization of the full [perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential); its curl contributes to the associated perturbed magnetic field. A gage transformation can change the vector-potential representation without changing this curl, so the vector-potential component is not uniquely identical to a magnetic-field component. The radial component provides an adjacent component specialization of the same perturbed-vector-potential family.

items.name: vertical_diamagnetic_current_density
items.description: Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of pressure-gradient-driven electric current per unit area along the toroidal symmetry axis in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of the diamagnetic contribution to [current density](name:current_density) onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents pressure-gradient-driven charge transport in the edge plasma.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},Z} = \hat{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing vertical height. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along increasing $Z$.

This quantity is the local algebraic sum of the vertical diamagnetic-current contributions from all included charge carriers and charge states; it is not species- or charge-state-resolved. It includes only the diamagnetic contribution, not the total vertical plasma current from all mechanisms, and implies neither spatial averaging nor integration.

The underlying vector has the magnitude given by [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density); the vertical projection is signed and is not that magnitude. It differs from [radial diamagnetic current density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density), which projects the same vector along increasing major radius, and from [parallel diamagnetic current density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density), which projects it along the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic current has a component in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: saturated_ion_current_density
items.description: Conventional ion charge flux per collecting area at a Langmuir-probe collector in the negative-bias saturation regime, where electron collection is suppressed.
items.documentation:
The saturated ion current density is the limiting conventional ion charge-flux density reaching a Langmuir-probe collector biased sufficiently negative relative to the plasma to suppress electron collection. It is the ion-saturation specialization of [ion current density](name:ion_current_density), rather than the unrestricted [current density](name:current_density) carried by all charged particles.

The charge-weighted ion flux defines the current-density vector:

$$
\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_a \sum_{z\geq 1} z e\,\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the saturated ion current-density vector, $i$ denotes the ion population, $a$ labels ion species, $z$ is the positive ionic charge number, $e$ is the elementary charge, and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is the particle-flux vector of that species and charge state at the collector in ion saturation.

The sum includes all collected ion species and charge states, weighted by their electric charge. Electron and neutral-particle contributions are excluded. This is a charge flux per collecting area, not an area-integrated current or an unweighted ion particle flux.

The [saturated ion current](name:saturated_ion_current) is the surface integral of the collector-directed component: $I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}=\int_S\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}\,dA$, where $I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the collected saturated ion current, $S$ is the collecting surface, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma into the collector. The [fluctuating saturated ion current density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density) is the temporal standard deviation of the collected current-density component; no temporal statistical operation is implied here.

Sign convention: Positive when positive ion charge flows from the plasma into the collector, as defined by the collector-directed normal.

items.name: helium_confinement_time
items.description: Characteristic e-folding time for the loss of confined thermalized helium-4 ash ions when their outward loss rate is proportional to the confined inventory.
items.documentation:
The global particle confinement time of thermalized helium-4 ash is the characteristic retention timescale for fully ionized helium-4 ions in the confined plasma. It describes particle loss from the total confined inventory, rather than the confinement of thermal energy or the survival of the plasma as a whole.

For source-free decay, the confinement time is defined by

$$
\frac{dN_{\mathrm{He}}}{dt}=-\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}}, \qquad \tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the total confined helium-4 ion inventory, $t$ is time, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}$ is the corresponding outward particle-loss rate. The definition assumes loss proportional to inventory and excludes helium sources during the decay interval. It is distinct from [energy confinement time](name:energy_confinement_time) and plasma confinement time.

items.name: ion_particle_source_rate
items.description: Ion particle source rate is the net contribution of ion production and removal to the particle-number balance of a specified ion population.
items.documentation:
Ion particle source rate is the signed contribution of ion production and removal to an ion population's particle-number balance. This shared concept encompasses local source terms, their explicit and density-proportional contributions, and volume-integrated rates.

The volume-integrated form is defined by

$$
S_i(V)=\int_V s_i\,dV'
$$

where $S_i(V)$ is the net ion particle source rate integrated over the plasma region $V$, $s_i$ is the local net volumetric [ion source rate](name:ion_source_rate), and $dV'$ is a physical volume element. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. In the cumulative form, $V$ is the entire volume enclosed by the specified magnetic flux surface. This integral is neither a flux-surface average nor the particle flux through that surface.

For a specified ion species, the source is summed over all ionic charge states without charge weighting. The [charge-state-resolved cumulative source rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate) restricts the enclosed-volume integral to one charge state. The [total ion particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate) additionally sums over all ion species. All contributing production and removal processes enter the net source; positive values indicate net addition and negative values indicate net removal. Transport across the region's boundary is a separate particle-balance contribution.

For the local decomposition, $s_i=s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}+\alpha_i n_i$, where $s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is the additive explicit source contribution independent of ion number density, $n_i$ is the number density of the considered ion population, and $\alpha_i$ is the [implicit ion particle source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). The implicit coefficient must be multiplied by density to give its local particle-production contribution; neither that coefficient nor the additive volumetric term alone is the volume-integrated rate.

items.name: normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface
items.description: Dimensionless minor-radius label of a magnetic flux surface, obtained by normalizing its major-radius half-width to a specified positive reference length.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the dimensionless minor-radius label assigned to a magnetic flux surface from its radial extent in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{minor}} = \frac{R_{\max}-R_{\min}}{2L_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $R_{\max}$ and $R_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum major-radius coordinates of the surface, each in m, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the specified positive reference length in m.

The label is a geometric normalization of the surface half-width; it is not a magnetic-flux normalization and therefore is distinct from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Its numerical value depends on the chosen reference length.

items.name: power_of_plant_system
items.description: Real electrical power assigned at a plant-system boundary, representing absorbed load, net generation balance, or an aggregate of included system loads.
items.documentation:
Real electrical power is the rate of electrical-energy transfer or accounting associated with a plant system at its electrical boundary. It excludes reactive power and other non-electrical energy flows.

The instantaneous power is defined by

$$
P = \frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $E$ is the electrical energy associated with the accounting boundary and $t$ is time.

The accounting convention is fixed by the specialized quantity. Absorbed power of a plant system represents one-way incoming electrical load, net power of a plant system represents generation minus internal consumption and is positive for net export, and total power of a plant system is the sum of the loads of all included systems. These forms are distinct applications of the same plant-boundary electrical-power concept.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the complex toroidal component of the first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the complex plasma magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the projection $\delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ along the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This imaginary part, $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$, together with the [real part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), fully specifies the complex toroidal component of the [perturbed plasma magnetic-field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) eigenfunction associated with a single toroidal mode number $n$ within the confined plasma region.

The full complex toroidal amplitude is decomposed as:

$$
\delta B_\phi = \mathrm{Re}(\delta B_\phi) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)
$$

where the ratio of imaginary to real parts encodes the spatial phase of the perturbation relative to the chosen eigenmode gage convention. The absolute magnitude of the eigenfunction is normalization-dependent and is set by the stability solver's normalization choice.

This quantity is defined within the confined plasma region and is computed alongside [poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) and radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part to fully characterize the phase-resolved perturbed magnetic-field vector inside the plasma. The vacuum-region counterpart for the same toroidal component is [toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part).

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$ is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_density
items.description: Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number density of a specified ion species, charge state, or population; a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state is summed over all charge states. It is not electric charge density or mass density.
items.documentation:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number density of the specified ion species, charge state, or population. It counts ions as particles and is distinct from electric charge density and mass density. For a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state, the density is summed over all charge states of that species represented in the same population scope.

The local differential definition is:

$$
n_i = \frac{dN_i}{dV}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $N_i$ is the number of ions in the specified population, and $V$ is physical volume.

For species $s$, the charge-state-summed convention is $n_{i,s} = \sum_Z n_{i,s,Z}$, where $n_{i,s,Z}$ is the ion number density of charge state $Z$ within the same species and population scope. A charge-state-resolved counterpart fixes $Z$ instead of applying this sum; [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) denotes such a quantity at its own stated population scope. Population-qualified forms restrict the same density concept, such as [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) for thermal ions and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) for suprathermal ions, while [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density) aggregates over ion species and [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is a spatial average of the local density.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description: Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium field. It excludes externally imposed vacuum perturbations when those are represented separately.
items.documentation:
Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium magnetic field. It represents magnetic-field bending and current perturbations inside the confined plasma and excludes any externally imposed vacuum perturbation that is retained as a separate field.

The plasma-response perturbation is defined by subtracting the equilibrium field and any separately represented vacuum perturbation from the total field in the confined plasma region:

$$
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathbf{x},t) = \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x},t) - \mathbf{B}_0(\mathbf{x}) - \delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, and $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the externally imposed vacuum magnetic perturbation that would exist without plasma response. If no separate vacuum perturbation is present or retained, set $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}=0$; the field satisfies $\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}=0$.

Externally imposed vacuum-field quantities, including [perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field), [radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field_at_control_surface, can drive the plasma response but are not included in $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ when represented separately. Fourier harmonic amplitudes, eigenfunction components, and spatial projections must carry their stated phase, harmonic, and direction definitions; they are not interchangeable with the unrestricted vector. The related component quantities [radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), [poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), and [toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) describe resolved quantities: radial is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, poloidal requires an explicitly defined poloidal projection direction such as the tangent to increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, and the toroidal entry denotes the single-harmonic $\hat{\phi}$-resolved quantity specified by that standard name.

Sign convention: Positive when a real resolved component of $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$, or the real part of a complex resolved component after applying its stated phase convention, is directed along the positive basis direction; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, $+\hat{R}$ is toward increasing major radius $R$, $+\hat{\phi}$ is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $+\hat{Z}$ is toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: power_due_to_fusion
items.description: Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified plasma region or material component. It counts fusion-product energy where it is deposited, not merely where it is released.
items.documentation:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified plasma region or material component is the rate at which energy whose ultimate source is fuel-ion fusion reactions is transferred to matter within that region or component. It is an extensive deposited-power quantity, so energy is assigned to the place where it is deposited, which may differ from the place where the fusion reaction occurred.

For a specified region or component $\Omega$, the quantity is defined by the local fusion-origin deposition rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\Omega) = \int_{\Omega} q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local rate density of energy deposited at position $\mathbf{x}$ by fusion products, fusion-neutron interactions, and secondary nuclear radiation, and $dV$ is the volume element of $\Omega$.

Each reaction channel contributes according to the partition of its released energy among products. For the deuterium-tritium channel, approximately one fifth of the fusion energy is born in the alpha particle and four fifths in the neutron; this birth partition does not imply local deposition. Charged-product energy is included in a plasma region only for the fraction actually deposited there during slowing down, while escaping charged products or neutrons contribute where they subsequently deposit energy through interactions and secondary radiation.

This name is distinct from [power density due to fusion](name:power_density_due_to_fusion), which denotes local fusion energy release rate before nonlocal transport, and from neutron power, which tracks energy carried by neutrons rather than deposited energy in $\Omega$. Power due to neutron interaction is the neutron-interaction contribution when the interacting neutrons originate from fusion. The divertor specializations [deposited power of divertor due to fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) and [power of divertor due to fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) restrict $\Omega$ to the divertor; non-fusion heat loads such as conduction, plasma radiation, charge-exchange neutrals, and externally supplied heating are excluded.

items.name: trapped_power_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the trapped orbit population, representing energy transfer to or from magnetically bouncing particles.
items.documentation:
Trapped power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is transferred to or from the trapped orbit population per unit physical volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of power density for particles whose parallel motion reverses at magnetic mirror points, so their guiding-center orbits bounce rather than circulate toroidally.

For a magnetic flux surface, the flux-surface-averaged trapped power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{tr}} = \left\langle \frac{dE_{\mathrm{tr}}}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped power density, $E_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the energy transferred to the trapped orbit population, $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average over that magnetic flux surface.

The scope is the trapped part of the particle distribution, with contributions from applicable heating and collisional energy-transfer processes. The aggregation convention is a net source term over those processes for the trapped orbit population on the flux surface; it is not a diagnostic-specific estimate, a point value before flux-surface averaging, or a total stored energy.

It excludes passing-orbit populations: [co-passing power density](name:co_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating in the co-current direction, and [counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating opposite to that direction. Together, trapped, co-passing, and counter-passing orbit-class power densities partition the orbit-resolved contribution to net plasma power density when defined for the same particle population and energy channels.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred to the trapped orbit population.

items.name: total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow momentum. The transported momentum density is the aggregate total, not an unspecified or single-population momentum channel.
items.documentation:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow momentum. This parent fixes the transported channel to total momentum: the momentum density is the population-summed aggregate of the constituent bulk-flow momentum densities included in the total-momentum balance, rather than an unspecified or single-population channel. Each component is a kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport direction, not a full viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$ along direction $\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for total momentum-density component $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}} = -\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\,\frac{\partial M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction $\hat{e}_i$ of the $j$ component of total bulk-flow momentum, $\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the directional total momentum diffusion coefficient, $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the $j$ component of total bulk-flow momentum density, $x_i$ is distance along $\hat{e}_i$, $i$ indexes the named transport direction, and $j$ indexes the momentum component. The minus sign defines the down-gradient diffusive contribution for a positive coefficient.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel, perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward increasing flux label.

This name is the total-momentum specialization of the [momentum diffusion coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and is the semantic parent of direction-qualified components such as the [poloidal total momentum diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from species- or population-qualified coefficients such as the [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and it is not the arithmetic sum of those coefficients; it relates the diffusive flux of aggregate total momentum to the gradient of aggregate total momentum density.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the temperature gradient of neutral particles in one internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
items.documentation:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar diffusivity that relates Fickian diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state to the temperature gradient of those same particles. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states, and is independent of any chosen spatial projection.

The isotropic Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s} \nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their number density, $D_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\nabla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

As the direction-agnostic parent, it is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: fast_ion_power_density
items.description: Volumetric rate of energy transfer from coherent radio-frequency waves to nonthermal fast ions of a selected species, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to the nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected ion species per unit physical volume. It describes spatially resolved wave absorption and also encompasses its flux-surface-averaged form.

The volumetric deposition rate is defined by

$$
Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{dP_i^{\mathrm{fast}}}{dV}
$$

where $Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion absorbed wave power density, $P_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the wave power absorbed directly by the fast population of ion species $i$, and $V$ is physical plasma volume.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species, not over different ion species. The [fast-ion charge-state power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) resolves the corresponding contributions by charge state or charge-state bundle. Direct absorption by thermal ions or electrons and subsequent collisional redistribution of the absorbed fast-ion energy are excluded.

This quantity is the fast-ion direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion power density](name:ion_power_density), rather than the full ion energy source from all processes. Flux-surface averaging preserves its recipient population and energy-transfer scope but is not required by this general definition. The [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density) further resolves the flux-surface-averaged deposition by toroidal Fourier harmonic.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description: Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium magnetic field. It is the poloidal projection of the [perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), rather than the unrestricted magnetic-field vector.

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x})\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

Here, $\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the chosen poloidal unit vector in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation after subtracting the equilibrium field and any separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbation. The complex quantity includes the [poloidal real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and [poloidal imaginary part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part); the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) is its complementary toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the perturbed magnetic field points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle within the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the signed flux through a horizontal disk centered on the symmetry axis and bounded by a toroidal circle through a boundary point.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the signed equilibrium flux through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by a toroidal circle through a boundary point. It is a locus-specific poloidal specialization of [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the boundary poloidal flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b} = \int_0^{R_b} B_Z(R',Z_b)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$ is the boundary poloidal magnetic flux, $R_b$ and $Z_b$ are the coordinates of a boundary point, $R'$ is the integration major radius, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component. The disk is oriented along the positive vertical unit vector $\hat{Z}$.

This definition applies to an axisymmetric equilibrium and includes contributions from both external sources and plasma current, rather than only [external magnetic flux](name:external_magnetic_flux). It differs from [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which threads the boundary-enclosed poloidal cross-section rather than a horizontal disk.

This is the boundary flux-function value, not the axis-to-boundary flux difference. Together with the magnetic-axis flux, it supplies the outer reference for poloidal-flux normalization; the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the plasma boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary) equals unity when those values define the normalization endpoints.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the defining disk is directed along $+\hat{Z}$.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.
